title: fix(kb): cross-process flock guards on shared KB working trees
description:
# Context

From the daemon-debate architectural analysis (.context/ox-daemon-debate.html): N per-repo daemons race on shared KB working trees at `~/.local/share/sageox/<endpoint>/kb/<kb_id>/`. The in-process kbReconcileLocks (sync_bubbles.go:35) is a sync.Map — useless across daemon processes. The GC os.Rename into .trash/ during another daemon's in-flight clone is the specific inode-yanked-out-from-under scenario.

This is Tier 1: silent data corruption. Distinct from Tier 2 (redundant API calls). Fix it independently and ahead of leader election.

# Scope

- `internal/daemon/sync_bubbles.go`: new `lockKBCheckout(kbID) (unlock func(), skipped bool)` using `syscall.Flock(fd, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)` on `~/.local/state/sageox/daemon/kb-locks/<kb_id>.lock`. Called at top of reconcileBubble before clone/pull.
- `internal/daemon/sync_gc_kb.go`: acquire same lock before any os.Rename into .trash/. GC must respect in-flight clones.
- Remove the in-process kbReconcileLocks sync.Map — the file lock subsumes it for cross-process AND in-process safety.
- Lock auto-releases on process death (kernel cleans up flock). No stale-lock recovery code.

# Acceptance

- [ ] TestKBReconcileCrossDaemonRace: spawn two daemons against the same endpoint, verify only one completes clone, other skips with EWOULDBLOCK.
- [ ] TestKBGCRespectsCloneInFlight: start clone in daemon A, fire GC triage in daemon B, verify GC skips that kb_id.
- [ ] TestKBLockReleasedOnCrash: kill daemon mid-clone, verify next daemon's next tick can acquire.
- [ ] No regression in single-daemon throughput (flock acquisition is microseconds on local FS).

# Parent

None directly. Connects to ADR-017 §5 (daemon spawn semantics). Companion to bead I (leader election). See `.context/ox-daemon-debate.html` PR1.
close_reason: Closed

title: supply-chain: SHA-256 verification of downloaded adapter binaries
description:
Threat model gap surfaced by /security-review port (see security/SECURITY.md #hunter-supply-chain → Open risks — flagged as 'single highest-impact gap in the model').

Current state: cmd/ox/adapter.go downloads adapter binaries from github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/... using browser_download_url verbatim from the GitHub API. verifyAdapterBinary (cmd/ox/adapter.go around line 452) runs './bin info' and confirms the JSON parses. This proves the binary is *some* ox adapter; it does not prove it is *the* adapter the registry intended.

Attack: a compromise of a GitHub release (push of a malicious replacement asset, account takeover, or CDN serve-time tampering) ships RCE to every 'ox adapter install' invocation. The 'nolint:gosec' markers at the http.Get sites are honest acknowledgements that this gap exists.

Acceptance:
- Each release ships a manifest.json containing per-asset SHA-256
- Manifest is fetched over a separate path (not from same release artifact list)
- Downloaded asset is verified against the manifest hash before being made executable
- Test that mutates one byte of a fixture binary asserts install fails with hash-mismatch error
- Threat model in security/SECURITY.md #hunter-supply-chain Open risks updated when shipped

Hard class: supply-chain-tampering (per security/config.yml — gets Opus validator)

title: secrets: heroku_key regex has no keyword guard, matches every UUIDv7
description: internal/session/secrets.go:201 'heroku_key' detector is a bare UUID regex [a-f0-9]{8}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[a-f0-9]{12} with no Keywords pre-screen. Comment acknowledges 'careful with false positives' and Redact is '[REDACTED_UUID]'. In real ledger: 2141 of 2155 dry-run matches (99.4%) are UUIDv7 session_id/agent_id values in session meta.json — not Heroku keys. Running ox session redact-history would replace these UUIDs in meta.json, corrupting session resolution across hundreds of sessions per .claude/rules/cache-only-design.md. Fix: add Keywords:['heroku'] guard OR tighten pattern to require heroku-specific context (e.g. preceded by 'heroku' or HEROKU_API_KEY=). Until fixed, redact-history is unsafe to run on any sageox ledger.

title: Pre-push hook: refuse to push Ledger commits containing known credential patterns
description:
## Problem

Forensic scan 2026-05-10 found 14 AWS STS tokens + 4 share-session cookies + 1 GitHub PAT + 16 Bearer headers staged in local Ledger files that are NOT YET pushed (`git log origin/main -- sessions/...` returns 0 commits for every affected session). A single `bd dolt push` or `ox session stop` with push enabled would publish all of them to `git.sageox.ai`.

Today, nothing stops that push.

## Fix

Install a pre-push step in ox CLI's Ledger push pipeline (NOT a global git hook — too easy to bypass). Before `git push` runs:
1. Compute `git diff origin/<branch>...HEAD --name-only` to enumerate files that would be pushed.
2. Run `DefaultPatterns` against each file's content as it exists in the local commit.
3. If any detector matches: fail loud with the detector name + file path + line number (NOT the secret value). Print remediation instructions: run `ox doctor --check=ledger-secrets`, edit the file, amend the commit (or use `ox session redact <sess_id>`).
4. Exit non-zero. Do not push.

## Bypass policy
- `--allow-secrets` flag for emergency overrides. Logs the override and prints a loud warning.
- The pre-push check is opinionated, not advisory: default is REFUSE.

## Acceptance
- Synthetic test: commit a file containing `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`, attempt push, assert push fails with the canary's detector name in the error.
- Same test with `--allow-secrets`: push succeeds.
- Performance: O(diff size), not O(repo size).
close_reason: Closed

title: Redact Authorization headers in data/github/pr/*.json cache writes
description:
## Problem

`repo_019c6d2e/data/github/2026/04/30/pr/1064-*.json` contains 16 `Authorization: Bearer <token>` headers across 8 cache files. The GitHub PR cache writer captures HTTP request headers verbatim and persists them to disk under the ledger-tracked `data/` path. **These files are tracked and pending push to the cloud Ledger.**

## Fix

Wherever ox CLI writes the GitHub PR cache (likely under `internal/github/` or `internal/data/github/` — confirm at impl), strip Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, X-Hub-Signature, and Proxy-Authorization headers from any captured request/response before serialization. Allowlist headers to KEEP rather than denylist to STRIP (safer).

## Acceptance
- Synthetic test: persist a captured request that includes `Authorization: Bearer test_token_value`; round-trip from disk and assert the header is absent (or replaced with `[REDACTED]`).
- Existing cache files are NOT auto-rewritten by this fix (that's a separate forensic-cleanup task — see scrub-existing-ledgers child); only new writes are clean.
close_reason: GitHub cache writer fields (Body/Title/Comments/commit msgs) now run through session.Redactor via injected FieldRedactor hook from cmd/ox/redactor_wiring.go init. Real leak path was user-authored text containing pasted curl examples, not HTTP-header capture in ox CLI itself. Tests in internal/ledger/github_data_test.go.

title: Fire redactor BEFORE cache write, not before commit
description:
## Problem

Forensic scan 2026-05-10:
- 19 session directories in `.sageox/cache/sessions/` contain credentials (staging)
- 16 session directories in `sessions/` contain credentials (committed)

The 3-session delta means the redactor is firing AFTER cache write — credentials reach disk in plaintext before redaction runs. If the user inspects `.sageox/cache/sessions/<ts>/raw.jsonl`, they see the raw secret. If a backup mirrors `.sageox/cache/`, the secret travels with it.

## Fix

Move redaction to the write path, not the commit path. Every `WriteEvent` / `AppendToTranscript` call should pass through `Redactor.Apply` before bytes hit `raw.jsonl`. The "commit" step (move from `.sageox/cache/` to `sessions/`) becomes a pure rename, no scrubbing required.

## Files
- Recorder write path (likely `internal/session/recorder.go` or `internal/session/capture.go` — confirm at implementation)
- `internal/session/secrets.go` — exports already exist (`DefaultPatterns`, `Redactor`)

## Acceptance
- Plant a known canary (`AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`) in a tool_result during an integration test.
- Read the resulting `.sageox/cache/sessions/<ts>/raw.jsonl` from disk.
- Assert the bytes contain `[REDACTED_AWS_KEY]` and do NOT contain `7EXAMPLE`.
- No live secret ever lands in any on-disk file under `.sageox/`.
close_reason: Closed

title: Extend internal/session/secrets.go detector set: sox_share_session, Authorization headers, GitLab variants, SageOx mk_, AgentX axk_
description:
## Problem

Forensic scan 2026-05-10 found credential classes leaking through session recordings that the existing detector set in `internal/session/secrets.go` does not catch:

| Class | Pattern | Real hits |
|---|---|---|
| SageOx share-session cookie | `sox_share_session=[A-Za-z0-9_-]{15,}` | 4 distinct values, 24 occurrences |
| Authorization: Bearer | `(?i)Authorization:\s*Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._=/+-]{20,}` | 16 occurrences in GitHub PR cache |
| Authorization: Basic | `(?i)Authorization:\s*Basic\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}` | 0 today, but symmetric with Bearer |
| GitLab OAuth | `gloas-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{15,}` | 0 today, but real token class |
| GitLab deploy / runner / feed | `gldt-`, `glrt-`, `glft-` | 0 today, real |
| SageOx API key | `mk_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}` | 0 today (good — but the detector must exist before any leak) |
| AgentX key | `axk_[A-Za-z0-9_]{32}` | 0 today, real |
| URL with embedded password | `https?://[^\s/:@]+:[^\s/:@]{6,}@` (with skip-list for `:x-oauth-basic@`, `:****@`, `[REDACTED]`) | 57 occurrences |
| `.env`-style assignment | `(?i)(API_KEY\|SECRET\|TOKEN\|PASSWORD\|PASSWD\|PWD)\s*=\s*['"]?[A-Za-z0-9_\-\.=/+]{12,}` | not measured, common in env-dump tool outputs |

## Fix

Add the patterns above to `DefaultPatterns()` in `internal/session/secrets.go`. Update `secrets_test.go` with positive + negative fixtures for each. Keep existing detector ordering (more-specific first) so prefix-anchored patterns win.

## Confidence calibration
- Prefix-anchored (mk_, axk_, gloas-, glpat-, sox_share_session=) → high confidence, no entropy filter.
- Authorization: Bearer → medium-confidence; flag but don't strip in shell help / docs (false-positive risk).
- URL-with-password → high confidence with explicit skip-list for OAuth basic patterns.
- .env-style → medium; require value of ≥12 chars to skip short test fixtures.

## Acceptance
- `secrets_test.go` table-driven entry per new pattern: hit + miss case.
- Existing detectors continue passing (no regression).
- Confirm `[REDACTED_*]` slugs are stable identifiers consumers can rely on (no version drift).
close_reason: Closed

title: Stop embedding GitLab PAT in .git/config origin URL by default
description:
## Problem

`internal/daemon/sync.go:1905-1930` (`injectGitCredentials`) and `internal/gitserver/remote.go:95` (`UpdateOriginCredentials`) explicitly embed the GitLab PAT into every Ledger's `origin` URL as `https://oauth2:TOKEN@git.sageox.ai/...`. This places the PAT into `.git/config` of every cloned Ledger.

Forensic scan 2026-05-10 found this PAT in 9 local Ledger configs spanning 58 days (first 2026-03-13). The same single PAT is shared across every Ledger; rotation requires rewriting every Ledger's origin URL.

## Fix

1. Add a git credential helper subcommand (e.g. `ox git-credential-helper`) backed by ox's existing credential store (`internal/gitserver/credentials*.go`).
2. On Ledger creation: write bare `origin` URL (no userinfo). Configure `[credential "https://git.sageox.ai"] helper = !ox git-credential-helper` in the Ledger's `.git/config`.
3. Stop calling `injectGitCredentials()` for persisted remotes. Reserve it for one-shot operations that need credentials inline (rare).
4. On daemon startup: walk every Ledger; if `origin` has embedded `oauth2:TOKEN@`, call `StripRemoteCredentials()` (`internal/gitserver/remote.go:197` — already implemented) once. Idempotent on re-runs.
5. Rotation pathway becomes: update credential store → no per-repo writes.

## Files
- `internal/daemon/sync.go:1905-1930`
- `internal/gitserver/remote.go:95-105, 197-220`
- `internal/gitserver/credentials*.go` (expose as credential helper)
- New: `cmd/ox/git_credential_helper.go`
- Existing Ledger migration: hook into daemon startup or new `ox doctor --fix` action

## Acceptance
- New `ox init` / Ledger clone leaves `origin` bare.
- `git remote -v` shows no embedded token on any Ledger.
- `git fetch` / `git push` still work (helper resolves auth).
- PAT rotation is a single credential-store write; no Ledger config writes.
close_reason: Credential helper subcommand (cmd/ox/git_credential_helper.go) + .git/config helper installer + daemon migration sweep all in place. Closes ox-np91 (PAT in .git/config). Outstanding: helper-protocol unit tests and migration tests — to follow with ox-yeae which adds the doctor check that exercises the same primitives.

title: Session-recording credential leak — close ox CLI writer-side + embed-side gaps
description:
## Context

Forensic scan of local Ledgers at ~/.local/share/sageox/sageox.ai/ledgers/ on 2026-05-10 confirmed multiple credential leak classes originating in ox CLI behavior. A prior real incident exposed credentials via a public/raw session artifact and led to **full account takeover of a SageOx user** (authenticated SageOx API access, private team/account data, GitLab token, read access to two private GitLab team-context repos).

## Scope (ox CLI only)

This epic covers the **ox CLI** side of the response. The sageox-monorepo PR covers the api-go authz fix (share-session entity-match) and the cloud-side scanner pipeline (Temporal nightly + backfill). The ox CLI changes here are independent — different repo, different blast radius — and would land as a separate PR.

## Findings to address

| # | Class | Where | Pushed to cloud? | Local-only risk? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | GitLab PAT `glpat-…` in `.git/config` `origin` URL of 9 local Ledgers | local working-copy metadata | No (config never pushed) | **Yes** — Time Machine, malware, shoulder-surf, `git remote -v` |
| F2 | 14 distinct AWS `ASIA…` STS tokens in `sessions/*/raw.jsonl` | ledger-tracked file | **Pending push** — `bd dolt push` / `ox session stop` publishes | n/a |
| F3 | 1 long-lived GitHub PAT in 2 session raw.jsonl | ledger-tracked | Pending push | n/a |
| F4 | 4 `sox_share_session=…` cookies in 2 session raw.jsonl | ledger-tracked | Pending push | n/a |
| F5 | 16 `Authorization: Bearer` headers in `data/github/PR/1064-*.json` cache | ledger-tracked | Pending push | n/a |
| F6 | 57 URL-embedded passwords (subset of F1 in git-push transcripts) | ledger-tracked | Pending push | n/a |

## Existing ox CLI assets to build on

- `internal/session/secrets.go` — already has 9+ detectors (AWS, GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Stripe, Twilio, SendGrid, …); needs new entries.
- `internal/gitserver/remote.go:197` — `StripRemoteCredentials()` already exists but is only invoked by doctor checks. Default code path embeds via `injectGitCredentials()` (`internal/daemon/sync.go:1905-1930`).
- ox already has a credential store at `internal/gitserver/credentials*.go`; not currently exposed as a git credential helper.
- Doctor framework can host new diagnostics (`cmd/ox/doctor_*.go`).

## Cross-repo references

- Related P1 epic: ox-x88q (daemon IPC + 3-agent security review) — different scope; this epic is the credential-leak-specific cut.
- sageox-monorepo plan: `~/.claude/plans/system-instruction-you-are-working-curried-prism.md` — covers api-go authz (WS-1) and scanner pipeline (WS-3) on the cloud side.
- Forensic timeline: F1 first leak 2026-03-13, F2-F5 first leak 2026-04-24, latest leak 2026-05-10 23:23 (today, still ongoing).

## Definition of done

1. No new session recording can land a known credential pattern in the cache or committed `sessions/` path.
2. No new Ledger setup writes the PAT into `.git/config`; existing Ledgers can be migrated to bare URL + credential helper.
3. `ox doctor` reports credential exposure in local Ledgers without uploading findings off-machine.
4. Pre-push hook refuses to publish a Ledger commit containing a known credential pattern.
5. Documented redaction set; documented recovery procedure when a credential slips through.
close_reason: All children closed. See per-child closures for implementation detail.

title: Bug: daemon Haiku 4.5 summarization consistently fails for recovered sessions
description: The daemon's anti-entropy summarization path (session_finalize.go BuildPrompt → InvokeClaude with Haiku 4.5) is failing for ALL recovered sessions since at least April 1. 40+ sessions affected, 96% failure rate overall. The error is always 'title too short (0 chars, minimum 3)' — meaning the LLM output either has no title or is unparsable. Only 2 of 21 May sessions have summaries, and both were summarized via the CLI path (ox session push-summary), not the daemon. The prompt asks Haiku to 'Read the session recording at: <path>' — the LLM appears unable to read the file and produce a valid JSON summary. Possible causes: (1) Haiku 4.5 in -p mode cannot reliably read large JSONL files. (2) The 10-minute timeout is insufficient for large sessions (some have 500+ entries / 300KB+). (3) The model returns conversational text instead of JSON. Need to check daemon logs for the actual LLM output being returned.
close_reason: Closed

title: P0: Daemon IPC has no peer authentication (SO_PEERCRED)
description:
Unix socket is mode 0600 but parent dir under ~/.local/state/sageox/daemon/ may have looser perms from earlier writers. No SO_PEERCRED/ucred check on accept. Any local process (rogue VS Code extension, browser via file://, another user on shared dev box) can drive checkouts, mutate sync state, trigger murmurs.

Locations:
- internal/daemon/ipc_unix.go:18-27
- internal/daemon/ipc_handlers.go (no auth on any handler)
- internal/paths/paths.go:512-519 (DaemonSocketFile)

Fix:
- On Linux: prefer $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/sageox/ (kernel-enforced 0700 per-user)
- Always: explicit os.Chmod(parent, 0700) even if dir already exists
- On accept: unix.Getsockopt(SO_PEERCRED) on Linux, LOCAL_PEERCRED on macOS — reject any UID != daemon owner
- Test: spawn daemon as user A, attempt connect as user B, expect rejection

DX cost: zero.
close_reason: SO_PEERCRED on Linux + LOCAL_PEERCRED on macOS via golang.org/x/sys/unix. Build-tagged files (ipc_peercred_{linux,darwin,windows,other}.go). handleConnection in internal/daemon/ipc.go now refuses connections where peerUID != os.Geteuid. Listen also chmods parent dir to 0700 even when it pre-existed with looser perms. peerCredDisabled escape hatch for tests; production code paths never set it. Tests cover same-process accept, non-Unix rejection, parent-dir chmod.

title: P0: Path-traversal RCE via attacker-authored meta.json filenames
description:
Attacker-controlled filename keys in meta.Files flow into filepath.Join(root, name) with no sanitization. Any teammate who can push a session can write arbitrary files (e.g. ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, ~/.config/sageox/auth.json) on every machine that hydrates. OID verification doesn't help — attacker chooses the OID.

Locations:
- cmd/ox/session_hydrate.go:124,138
- internal/lfs/meta.go:306,338,403
- cmd/ox/import.go:296
- cmd/ox/memory_put.go:135
- internal/lfs/pointer.go (WritePointerFiles)

Fix:
- Add lfs.SafeRelativeName(s) error helper rejecting:
  - filepath.Clean(s) != s
  - contains '..'
  - leading '/' or '\\'
  - filepath.IsAbs(s)
- Call from ReadSessionMeta, WritePointerFiles, ResolveContentPath, import paths, memory writers
- Add regression test TestMeta_RejectsPathTraversalFilenames covering each entrypoint

DX cost: zero — legitimate filenames unaffected.

Real exploitability: HIGH. Session sync is automatic; ox session download is documented and routinely invoked. Single compromised teammate token escalates to RCE on every hydrating machine.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #579 on ryan/sec branch

title: ox-adapter-claude-code: gut hook installer (writes invalid string-format hooks that Claude Code rejects)
description:
cmd/ox-adapter-claude-code/hooks.go writes hooks as bare strings (hooks[event] = hookCmd at line 45 of handleInstallHooks). Claude Code's settings parser rejects this format with 'PostToolUse: Expected array, but received string' and skips the entire settings file.

The built-in InstallProjectClaudeHooks (cmd/ox/hooks_claude.go:295) already installs the same events in the correct array format. The external adapter is duplicating + clobbering.

Fix: remove CapHookInstaller from the adapter manifest, OR remove handleInstallHooks/handleCheckHooks/handleUninstallHooks entirely. Verify init.go's installAgentHooks no longer calls into the adapter for hook ops.

Acceptance: After ox init in a fresh dir, .claude/settings.json passes Claude Code's parser (every hook event is an array of {matcher, hooks: [{type, command}]} entries — never a bare string).

Parent: ox-hs1b
acceptance_criteria: settings.json passes Claude Code parser; no string-format hooks anywhere in output; existing tests still green; new contract test covers it
close_reason: Adapter hook handlers neutered to no-ops; built-in InstallProjectClaudeHooks remains authoritative. Verified by package tests.

title: Test PreToolUse stdout injection in Claude Code
description: Empirically verify whether PreToolUse hook stdout is injected into Claude Code's model context. Currently phaseBeforeTool is a noop (activePhaseBehavior excludes it) and was never tested — the empirical testing table in agent_hook.go:38-47 covers UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart, PreCompact but NOT PreToolUse. If stdout IS visible to the model, this is the best mid-turn whisper delivery channel (fires before every tool execution, mid-turn, model still processing). title: fix codedb indexing loop: CheckFreshness race + bleve lock-timeout nuke
description:
Two bugs combine to cause a perpetual indexing loop that burns CPU and never completes.

**Bug 1: CheckFreshness race** — m.indexing is read-then-check but not set until inside Index(). Window allows multiple goroutines to launch concurrently. Each one that loses the race returns 'indexing already in progress' and calls gcDirtyIndexes(dataDir), which leads to Bug 2.

**Bug 2: gcDirtyIndexes destroys active bleve index** — gcDirtyIndexes calls codedb.Open() which calls openOrCreateBleveIndex which calls safeOpenBleve. The active goroutine holds bbolt's exclusive file lock. safeOpenBleve fails with a lock-timeout error (NOT bleve.ErrorIndexPathDoesNotExist). openOrCreateBleveIndex misinterprets this as corruption and calls os.RemoveAll(bleveCodeDir), deleting the bleve index being actively written. The winning goroutine's next batch write (at checkpoint ~50 commits) hits ENOENT → fails → loop repeats.

**Fix 1**: In CheckFreshness, set m.indexing = true before launching the goroutine (inside the existing mutex block). Extract index body to avoid double-guard conflict.

**Fix 2**: In openOrCreateBleveIndex, before nuking, check if root.bolt exists. If bolt file exists, the error is likely lock contention, not corruption — return error without nuking.

**Fix 3**: Add failure-mode tests: (1) CheckFreshness called rapidly does not spin up multiple goroutines, (2) openOrCreateBleveIndex does not nuke when bolt is locked by another open.
close_reason: fixed CheckFreshness race (set m.indexing before goroutine, extracted doIndex), fixed openOrCreateBleveIndex to not nuke on lock timeout, added regression tests

title: Fix+Test: sparse-checkout set must not remove staged files outside cone
description: sparse-checkout set removes tracked files outside the cone from the working tree. If the CLI stages files in data/custom/ or data/linear/ and the daemon reconfigures sparse checkout before commit, those staged files are deleted from disk. Fix: detect dirty dirs outside cone and include them in the set. Test: stage files in data/custom/, reconfigure, assert files survive.
close_reason: Fixed: dirtyDirsOutsideCone() detects staged/modified files in dirs outside the computed cone and adds them to the sparse set before calling sparse-checkout set. Added 3 tests: 2 unit (PreservesStagedFilesOutsideCone, PreservesModifiedFilesOutsideWindow) in murmur_test.go, 1 integration (PreservesStagedFilesOutsideCone) in sync_ledger_test.go.

title: codedb: indexing runs indefinitely when worktree deleted
description:
IndexLocalRepo has no timeout and runs forever against deleted worktree paths. A Copenhagen-v4 worktree was deleted by Conductor but the daemon kept its indexing goroutine alive for 21+ hours, burning 134-198% CPU the entire time.

## Root Causes
1. CheckFreshness passes the daemon lifetime context — no indexing-specific timeout
2. No upfront existence check on projectRoot before starting go-git
3. UpdateProjectRoot resets m.dataDir on every heartbeat, causing unnecessary churn

## Fix
1. Add 2h timeout context in CheckFreshness goroutine
2. Check os.Stat(projectRoot) at start of Index(), return error immediately if missing
3. Remove m.dataDir reset from UpdateProjectRoot (dataDir is per-repo, stable across worktrees)
close_reason: Fixed: fail-fast on deleted projectRoot, 2h timeout in CheckFreshness, removed unnecessary dataDir reset in UpdateProjectRoot

title: cli_hours_active_7d overcounts: CountCLIActivityHours counts rows, not distinct hours
description:
VERIFIED BUG, independent of the repo_id issue and arguably worse.

apps/api-go/internal/db/queries/auth.sql:17-22:
  -- name: CountCLIActivityHours :one
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS hours FROM cli_activity WHERE user_id = $1 AND hour_bucket >= $2;

It counts ROWS. The dedup key is (user_id, COALESCE(repo_id,''), hour_bucket), so one user in one hour produces 1 NULL row + 1 row per repo whose detail was fetched.

CONCRETE: a single 'ox status' in an initialized project fires GET /cli/repos/{repo_id} (status.go:422) AND GET /cli/repos (status.go:426) back to back -> 2 rows in one hour bucket -> reported as 2 hours active.

BLAST RADIUS: cli_auth.go:200 feeds this into analytics.Identify as the PostHog PERSON PROPERTY cli_hours_active_7d (analytics.go:205). Wrong value propagates into every cohort, funnel and activation metric keyed on it.

FALSIFIABLE CHECK: the 7d window has 168 hours. Any user with cli_hours_active_7d > 168 proves the metric is broken. Run that query first.

FIX: COUNT(DISTINCT hour_bucket). One line + sqlc regen. Note isFirstRun/isReactivated in cliactivity.go are 0-vs-nonzero checks and are NOT affected.
notes:
ALREADY FIXED server-side on misc-coe branch ajit/misc-coe, commit 8b321224c:
  -SELECT COUNT(*) AS hours
  +SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT hour_bucket) AS hours
plus the regenerated sqlc/auth.sql.go. Comment updated to 'Count distinct wall-clock hours, not per-repo rows within each hour.' Exactly the recommended fix. Not yet merged to main — verify it lands before trusting cli_hours_active_7d.
close_reason: Fixed server-side on ajit/misc-coe commit 8b321224c; tracking merge separately

title: cli_activity.repo_id means 'the URL named a repo', not 'the user worked in a repo'
description:
ROOT CAUSE (verified): cliactivity.go:77-81 sets repo_id ONLY from chi.URLParam(r,'repo_id'). TrackActivity is mounted on exactly one route group (router.go:2020, /api/v1/cli/*), and only ONE route in it has a {repo_id} param: GET /cli/repos/{repo_id}. Every other tracked route -- GET /cli/repos, GET /cli/doctor/context, POST /cli/friction, POST /cli/repo/init -- is structurally NULL.

So 68% NULL is not data loss, it is the schema working as designed. The column answers 'did the URL name a repo' while every consumer reads it as 'was the user active in this repo'.

DOWNSTREAM (verified): hq.sql GetCLIActivityScalars computes active_repos and active_teams as COUNT(DISTINCT repo_id) WHERE repo_id IS NOT NULL -- both undercount to only the repo-detail fetches.

FIX DIRECTION: ox knows config.GetRepoID(projectRoot) on every invocation but never puts it on the wire (useragent.SetHeaders sends only User-Agent, X-Orchestrator, traceparent). Send repo identity as a header; middleware prefers path param, falls back to header. Cross-repo + new wire contract -> needs Ryan review per CLAUDE.md 'API source of truth'.
notes:
CLI SIDE SHIPPED (ox repo, branch ajit/fix-telemetry-daemon). The header is INERT until api-go reads it.

WIRE CONTRACT — what ox now sends:
  Header: X-Sageox-Repo-Id
  Value:  the SageOx repo ID from .sageox/config.json (config.GetRepoID)
  Shape:  ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$  (validated CLI-side before emit)
  Sent on: every SageOx API request built through useragent.SetHeaders /
           useragent.NewRequest — internal/api, internal/auth,
           internal/doctorapi, internal/telemetry. Not git/LFS transport.
  Omitted (never empty) when: outside a project, repo not yet registered,
           value fails validation, or the process is the daemon.

DAEMON IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. It serves every workspace on the machine
from one process, so a process-global repo ID would stamp all its traffic
with whichever repo it started in — wrong data, not missing data. Daemon
rows stay repo-less. Regression test: internal/cli/repoid_test.go
TestNewContext_DaemonIsNotTaggedWithRepoID.

REMAINING api-go WORK (needs Ryan review — new wire contract):
  middleware/cliactivity/cliactivity.go, replace lines 77-81:
    if id := chi.URLParam(r, "repo_id"); id != "" {
        repoID = pgtype.Text{String: id, Valid: true}      // path wins
    } else if id := r.Header.Get("X-Sageox-Repo-Id"); id != "" {
        repoID = pgtype.Text{String: id, Valid: true}      // fall back
    }
  Re-validate server-side (do NOT trust the client's character class) and
  consider verifying the caller actually has access to that repo before
  storing it — the header is user-controlled input.

  Note the dedup key is (user_id, COALESCE(repo_id,''), hour_bucket), so
  once the header lands, hours that used to produce one NULL row will
  produce one repo row instead. That CHANGES the row shape feeding
  CountCLIActivityHours — fix ox-5bz3 (COUNT DISTINCT) at the same time or
  cli_hours_active_7d will shift for reasons unrelated to real usage.

title: ox daemon start --foreground poisons command latency telemetry
description: The daemon process runs as 'ox daemon start --foreground'. Cobra's PersistentPostRunE fires TrackCommandCompletion when it finally exits, reporting the entire daemon lifetime as command duration (p50 70min, max 8.8 days). Same for the OTel root span. Fix: mark long-running service invocations and skip CLI command instrumentation for them.

title: Fix OTLP exporter 401: attach JWT Bearer per-request
description: PR #1217 in sageox-monorepo (commit 4bc7356c3) JWT-gated /api/v1/otlp/* on 2026-05-14. CLI+daemon OTLP exporters in internal/observability/otel.go construct the otlptracehttp exporter with no auth header, so /api/v1/otlp/v1/traces returns 401 and trace batches are silently dropped (~174k 401s in last 30d Honeycomb). Fix: attach an auth RoundTripper via otlptracehttp.WithHTTPClient that pulls the current token from the local token store per-request (handles daemon long-running token rotation). Keep existing telemetry/endpoint gate; do not roll back server JWT-gating (intentional per audit ox-w9yc5).

title: [HUMAN] kb config: revisit committed_at + banner with sageox-mono team (time-sensitive)
description:
# Context

The mono PR (`sageox-mono` branch `ryan/kb-config`) is approved but unmerged. Its `.sageox/config.yaml` envelope carries:
1. A multi-line 'THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH' banner.
2. A `committed_at` field as a monotonic ordering guard for out-of-order webhook deliveries.

Both add noise and aren't actually needed. Easier to revise now than after rollout.

# Why this is wrong

**The banner:** doesn't survive hand-edits, bloats every diff (first ~10 lines of every file-level change), generates merge friction, and teaches nothing the schema and ADR already do. Tools that pretend the banner is load-bearing get falsified the first time someone deletes it. Drop it.

**`committed_at`:** redundant with git metadata. Every property the in-file field provides is provided more truthfully by git:
- 'Is this newer than what Postgres has?' → `git log -1 --format=%cI` on `.sageox/config.yaml`
- 'Did I already process this push?' → compare commit SHAs; or `git merge-base --is-ancestor <stored> <incoming>`
- Out-of-order webhook drops → same compare, but value is server-attested by git, not writer-attested by whoever last edited the YAML.

In-file `committed_at` is **trustless metadata pretending to be authoritative**. Anyone hand-editing the file can put any value there. The whole reason to put source-of-truth in git is that git's metadata is trusted; re-encoding a timestamp inside the file then trusting THAT timestamp gives back the property we just bought.

Counter ('readers without git access'): weak. Postgres can carry `last_synced_sha` as a column populated from git. HTTP responses can include commit metadata as a sibling field. Neither requires embedding in the config blob.

# Ask

1. Drop the banner generation from `packages/kb/config_yaml.go` `MarshalConfigYAML`.
2. Replace in-file `committed_at` with: reconcile activity compares git commit SHAs from webhook payload; Postgres mirror carries `last_synced_sha` + `last_synced_commit_at` columns derived from git metadata, not from inside the config blob.
3. Update the YAML parser to gracefully ignore both fields if present (so existing files keep working through any transition).

# Time-sensitivity

The branch is approved (ADR-031 Amendment 1 signed by Ryan + Ajit on 2026-05-18) but not merged. Easier to revise the design now than after the file format ships to prod and tools+tests calcify around it.

# Owner

Ryan to coordinate with the mono team (Ajit). Suggest a 15-min sync to revisit before merge.

title: feat(daemon): leader-elect per-(user, endpoint) global-sync owner via flock lease
description:
# Context

From the daemon-debate architectural analysis: N per-repo daemons redundantly poll `/api/v1/kb` and `/api/v1/cli/repos` every 15s. The user observed competing daemons running global sync N times. Fix: elect one daemon per (user, endpoint) tuple as the global-sync owner via a file-locked lease. Non-owners skip the global API + sync passes.

This is Tier 2 (redundant API calls). Should ship AFTER bead H (race fix) bakes in production.

# Scope

- New file `internal/daemon/global_lease.go` exporting AcquireGlobalSyncLease(endpoint) (*Lease, error) and Lease.Release(). Implementation: flock(2) LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB on `~/.local/state/sageox/<endpoint>/global-sync.lease`. Returns ErrNotOwner if held.
- Acquire on daemon startup; store on daemon struct; release on shutdown / process exit (kernel handles flock cleanup).
- Gate the team-context and KB sync tickers on `if d.lease != nil { ... }`. Per-repo work (ledger, index, sessions, whispers) stays unguarded.
- Update `~/.local/state/sageox/daemon/registry.json` to include `global_sync_owner: bool` per daemon.
- New doctor check `kb-global-sync-no-owner`: for each endpoint with ≥1 running daemon, exactly one must be owner. AutoFix: nudge lowest-PID daemon to retry acquisition.
- Lease held for daemon lifetime (not per-tick). Failover on owner death is automatic via flock semantics.

# Acceptance

- [ ] Two daemons against same endpoint → exactly one runs the API list call.
- [ ] Kill owner → other becomes owner within one tick interval.
- [ ] No flock races on local filesystem.
- [ ] Doctor check surfaces no-owner state and auto-repairs.

# Parent

None directly. ADR-017 §5. Depends on bead H.

# Depends on

- ox-kdt2 (kb-id flock as the primitive that proves flock semantics work for our use case)
close_reason: Closed

title: ox: ox doctor migration of project-side .sageox/config.json → .yaml (hybrid + staged deprecation)
description:
# Context

title: ox: ResolveSessionRecording integrates ResolveCurrentKB + safety inversion
description:
# Context

The existing ox-43q0.3 task assumed the resolver existed and the precedence chain consumed it. Per /grill-me, that resolver is being built (bead A) and the safety-inversion logic vendored (bead B). This bead is the integration point.

This supersedes ox-43q0.3 — it preserves the goal but uses the new resolver and vendored ResolveEffectiveMode rather than ad-hoc per-source code.

# Scope

- Update `internal/config/session_recording.go` `ResolveSessionRecording()`:
  - Use ResolveCurrentKB (bead A) to determine the current KB.
  - Use vendored ResolveEffectiveMode (bead B) for safety-inversion-aware precedence.
  - Layers (low → high): default-per-KB-type → user config → KB local (.sageox/config.yaml) → OX_SESSION_RECORDING env.
  - Safety inversion: if EITHER user-level OR KB-level is 'disabled', effective is 'disabled' regardless of precedence. Use ResolveEffectiveMode for this.
  - Surface a `ResolvedSessionRecording.Source` field showing which layer won (for ox kb config get --show-origin and ox doctor).
- All session-start paths that today check IsInitialized + read legacy ledger config switch to using this resolver.

# Acceptance

- [ ] Unit tests for each precedence layer (mock vendored types and the resolver).
- [ ] Unit tests for safety inversion: user=auto + kb=disabled → disabled; user=disabled + kb=auto → disabled.
- [ ] Integration test in `cmd/ox/` confirming session-start respects the resolver.
- [ ] Source field accurate in all matrix cases.

# Parent

ox-43q0. Supersedes ox-43q0.3.

# Depends on

- ox-z526 (resolver)
- ox-jzlm (vendored types)
close_reason: Closed

title: ox: ox kb config get/list with --show-origin/--at/--json (read-only, no set)
description:
# Context

Per /grill-me Q4: drop ox kb config set entirely. Keep get and list as read-only CLI verbs. All writes happen via hand-edit + git push OR the web UI; ox is read-only for KB config (except the doctor migration in F).

Per /grill-me Q10: reads come from the LOCAL FILE only (no API fallback). The daemon keeps the local file fresh; if a KB hasn't synced yet, return an actionable error.

This supersedes ox-43q0.5 which proposed get/set/list.

# Scope

- New CLI command `ox kb config get <key> [--kb=<slug>] [--show-origin] [--at=<scope>] [--json]`
- New CLI command `ox kb config list [--kb=<slug>] [--show-origin] [--json]`
- Effective resolution uses vendored `ResolveEffectiveMode` from B; precedence is default → user → KB local → env, with safety inversion for session_recording.
- `--show-origin` displays which layer won, with `[trigger]` annotation when safety inversion is the cause (vs standard precedence).
- `--at=<scope>` returns only the value stored at the named scope (kb | user | env | default).
- `--kb=<slug>` accepts bare slug or `#`-prefixed; strip the `#` before resolution.
- If `--kb` omitted, uses ResolveCurrentKB(cwd). If no current KB, error with a helpful message.
- Cold-start: if KB's `.sageox/config.yaml` doesn't exist locally, error with 'KB has no local clone yet. Wait for next daemon sync (≤15s), or run ox doctor --check=kb-stale-sync.' Do NOT fall back to API.

# Acceptance

- [ ] All flag combinations have integration tests (table-driven, against fixtures).
- [ ] Safety-inversion display matches the [trigger] annotation pattern from /grill-me Q4.
- [ ] JSON output schema documented inline.
- [ ] No write code paths anywhere in this bead's surface.

description:

title: ox: internal/kb.ResolveCurrentKB resolver + .sageox/ marker parsing
description:
# Context

ADR-017 establishes the Knowledge Bubble (KB) as the canonical workspace primitive. This task implements the resolver that maps a filesystem path to its bound KB (or nil).

# Scope

- New file `internal/kb/resolve.go` exporting:
  - `type KBBinding struct { KBID, KBType, Slug, Endpoint, Source, Anchor, Scope string }`
  - `func ResolveCurrentKB(cwd string) (*KBBinding, error)` — walks up from cwd looking for `.sageox/` markers, returns the nearest binding or `(nil, nil)` if none found.
  - `func (b *KBBinding) IsWorkspace() bool` — true if cache/ledger/symlinks exist alongside `config.yaml`.
- Marker priority within a directory: `.sageox/config.yaml` > `.sageox/config.json` (legacy).
- The `endpoint:` field in the YAML is optional. If absent, fall back to `endpoint.Get()`.
- Subtree overrides (a nested `.sageox/` inside another) reserved — return clear error in v1.
- Resolver must also resolve `kb_type`/`slug` from the kb-API (or cached merger output) given the `kb_id` — these aren't in the file.

# Acceptance

- [ ] `ResolveCurrentKB` table-driven tests covering: nil case, workspace case, binding-only case, multi-level nesting (nearest wins), endpoint-explicit vs endpoint-fallback, both legacy `.json` and new `.yaml` formats.
- [ ] `IsWorkspace()` correctly distinguishes workspace from binding-only.
- [ ] No symlink-resolution traps (use Go stdlib `filepath` defaults — don't try to be clever).
- [ ] Documented as the only sanctioned answer to "which KB am I in"; existing call sites that path-walk for `.sageox/` get a follow-up task to migrate.

# Parent

ox-43q0 (KB config epic). ADR-017.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add 'ox kb config get/set/list' commands (git config-style UX)
description:
Implement new CLI commands modeled after `git config`. Vocabulary should be intentionally familiar.

# Commands

## ox kb config get <kb-id> [<key>]
- No key: pretty-print full effective config with source annotations (like `git config --list --show-origin`).
- With key (e.g., `features.session_recording.mode`): print just that value + its source tier (env/user/kb/team/default).
- `--json` flag for machine-readable output.

Example:
```
$ ox kb config get kb_01H... features.session_recording.mode
auto    (source: kb-config)
```

## ox kb config set <kb-id> <key> <value>
- Validates against the vendored schema before sending.
- PATCHes `/api/v1/kb/{kb-id}/config` with the minimal nested object.
- On success, prints the new effective value and the commit SHA from the KB git repo (server returns this in the PATCH response per the mono PR).
- Requires KB admin role; server returns 403 otherwise — surface a clear message.

## ox kb config list
- Lists all KBs the user is a member of with their current config (or just the differentiating fields). Could ship as `ox kb config list --all` in a follow-up.

## ox kb config unset <kb-id> <key>
- PATCH with explicit null to remove the key from KB config (falls back to default per type).

# Placement

Under `cmd/ox/kb_config.go` (or similar). Register as subcommands of an existing `kb` command group; create the group if it doesn't exist.

# Acceptance

- All four commands wired up + help text.
- `--json` output for `get` and `list`.
- Validation rejects invalid mode values before network call.
- Integration test against test environment: set → get round-trip.
- Help text references the git-config analogy explicitly so the mental model carries over.

Depends on KB-API client task.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add KB-API tier to ResolveSessionRecording precedence chain
description:
Extend `internal/config/session_recording.go` `ResolveSessionRecording()` to add a new tier: **KB-API config**, sitting between project-local file (`.sageox/config.yaml`) and team config.

New precedence (low → high):
1. Default per KB type (auto for personal/team/repo, manual for profile/custom/channel)
2. Team config
3. **KB-API config (new)** — `client.GetKBConfig(ctx, kbID).Features.SessionRecording.Mode`
4. Project config (`.sageox/config.yaml` locally)
5. User config (`~/.config/sageox/config.yaml`)
6. `OX_SESSION_RECORDING` env var

**Safety inversion:** if EITHER the user-level OR KB-level setting is `disabled`, the effective mode is `disabled`. This overrides standard precedence — it's a privacy/safety floor. Implement as a final pass after standard precedence resolution.

KB ID resolution: the CLI determines which KB a session targets via existing logic (`ox session start` knows the KB context). Reuse that resolver; this task is purely about the precedence chain.

Acceptance:
- Unit tests for each tier (mock KB-API client, set/unset each layer).
- Unit test for safety inversion: user=auto + KB=disabled → effective=disabled. User=disabled + KB=auto → effective=disabled.
- `ResolvedSessionRecording` struct gains a `Source` field showing which tier won (for debugging / `ox kb config get --show-origin`).

Depends on schema vendoring + KB-API client tasks.

title: Epic: ox CLI integration with unified KB config (kb config like git config)
description:
# Context

Cross-repo coordination with sageox/sageox-monorepo. The mono repo is adding a unified per-Knowledge-Bubble configuration system stored in `.sageox/config.yaml` inside each KB's git repo (Postgres mirrors as a cache). This epic tracks the ox CLI side: consume the new config, expose it via CLI commands, and unify session-recording precedence.

# Mental model

`kb config` is to a `.sageox/` KB repo what `git config` is to a `.git/` repo. Adopt that vocabulary explicitly in command names and docs:

| git config | kb config |
|---|---|
| /etc/gitconfig | (future) org/team defaults |
| ~/.gitconfig | ~/.config/sageox/config.yaml |
| .git/config | .sageox/config.yaml |
| git config --local <k> <v> | ox kb config set <kb-id> <k> <v> |
| git config --global <k> <v> | ox config set <k> <v> |
| git config --list | ox kb config get <kb-id> (effective + sources) |

Precedence (low→high): defaults-per-KB-type → user config → KB config → `OX_SESSION_RECORDING` env.

**Safety inversion:** for the `session_recording` setting, both user *and* KB admin have veto power. A user's `disabled` overrides a KB's `auto`. A KB's `disabled` overrides a user's `auto`. This is a privacy guarantee, not standard precedence.

# Schema

The canonical schema lives in sageox-monorepo `packages/kb/config.go` `KBConfig`. The mono PR will emit a generated JSON Schema to `packages/kb-types/schema.json` for ox CLI to consume.

Key new field:
```yaml
features:
  session_recording:
    mode: auto | manual | disabled
  murmurs:
    enabled: true | false
  visibility: private | team
```

Defaults per KB type (matches `DefaultSessionRecordingMode` in mono):
- personal, team, repo: `auto`
- profile, custom, channel: `manual`

# Workspace for implementation

**This work happens in `/Users/ryan/conductor/workspaces/ox/charlotte-v7`**, not in the user's primary checkout. Beads sync via Dolt so this epic and its children will be visible from charlotte-v7.

# Dependencies on sageox-monorepo

The mono PR ships:
1. New tri-state `session_recording.mode` field in KBConfig.
2. `.sageox/config.yaml` in KB git tree (source of truth) + Postgres mirror (read cache).
3. `PATCH /api/v1/kb/{id}/config` accepts the new shape.
4. Generated `packages/kb-types/schema.json`.
5. ADR-031 amendment for the new file in `.sageox/`.

Order: ox CLI can develop against a mock API or stub schema. For e2e smoke, the mono PR must be deployed to test first.

# Today's state in ox CLI

- `internal/config/session_recording.go` already has tri-state `[disabled, manual, auto]` constants and `ValidSessionRecordingModes`.
- `ResolveSessionRecording(projectRoot)` resolves env → user → project (`.sageox/config.json`) → team → default.
- `internal/config/project_config.go` reads `.sageox/config.json` (JSON, not YAML).
- `internal/config/murmuring.go` has a parallel `ResolveMurmuring` and mtime-style cache pattern.
- `cmd/ox/config_settings.go` has a settings registry with `ConfigLevel` enum (User/Repo/Team).

# What changes

- Add a 4th precedence tier: **KB-API config** (queries the SageOx API for the KB's effective config). Sits between project (local file fallback) and team. The API itself reads from Postgres mirror of `.sageox/config.yaml`.
- Migrate `.sageox/config.json` to `.sageox/config.yaml` (YAML preserves comments — humans hand-edit this file).
- Add `ox kb config get/set/list` commands.
- Add JSON Schema validation against the generated schema from sageox-monorepo.

# Acceptance criteria

- `ox kb config get <kb-id>` shows effective config + source of each value (like `git config --show-origin`).
- `ox kb config set <kb-id> session_recording disabled` PATCHes the API; change visible in console KB Settings page; commit appears in KB repo's `.sageox/config.yaml` history.
- `ResolveSessionRecording` in CLI consults KB API tier; offline mode falls back to cached `.sageox/config.yaml` from last sync.
- Existing `.sageox/config.json` continues to work for one release (deprecation warning).
- Schema validation catches malformed `.sageox/config.yaml`.
- E2E: set KB to `disabled` via console → CLI in that workspace refuses to record → no fight with user override.

# Out of scope

- Org-level / team-level config inheritance (future).
- Migration of other ProjectConfig fields (github_sync, recording_reminder) to the new tier — covered by separate beads once this lands.

title: Supersede shutdown race deletes new daemon's socket file
description:
When two ox daemons share the same repo_id, they map to the same workspace_id and same socket path. During supersede, the old daemon's IPC server runs cleanupSocket() on ctx cancellation (internal/daemon/ipc.go:1486), which os.Remove()s the file at the shared path — but that file now belongs to the new daemon. Result: new daemon is running but unreachable (in-kernel socket survives, on-disk path is gone). Next ListRunningDaemons() prunes its registry entry. ox murmur and other CLI calls then report 'daemon unavailable'. Reproduced in ~/Code/sageox/sageox-design.

Fix: stop unlinking the socket in Server.Start shutdown. Daemon.cleanup() already owns socket-file lifetime and respects wasSuperseded. Pre-bind os.Remove in listen() stays unchanged.

See plan: /Users/ryan/.claude/plans/system-instruction-you-are-working-recursive-coral.md
notes:
Root cause turned out to be two layers:
1. cleanupSocket(socketPath) in Server.Start after ctx.Done() — removed.
2. **The real culprit:** Go's *net.UnixListener.Close() auto-unlinks the socket file by default. Added SetUnlinkOnClose(false) in listen() so the listener never unlinks; ownership now lives solely in Daemon.cleanup (which respects wasSuperseded).

Regression test in internal/daemon/server_shutdown_test.go:
- TestServerStart_DoesNotRemoveSocketOnShutdown verifies the listener-close + Server.Start path preserves the socket file (failed without the SetUnlinkOnClose fix; cleanupSocket removal alone was not enough)
- TestDaemonCleanup_SupersededPreservesSocket pins the Daemon.cleanup branch invariant.

Pre-bind unlink in listen() unchanged — that path stays so the next daemon to start can bind cleanly.

title: Implement /security-review AI security pipeline (ox CLI)
description:
SageOx /security-review pipeline tailored for the ox CLI repo. Sister epic to sageox-mono ox-557ft (which has the deep design rationale, Dependency-Track infra, and shared design decisions).

Source article: https://www.synthesia.io/post/automating-code-security-reviews-with-claude-mythos-level-capabilities

## Why a SEPARATE epic (not "do the same thing")

The ox CLI threat model is meaningfully different from the monorepo:

| Concern | Monorepo | ox CLI |
|---|---|---|
| Distribution | Internal (test.sageox.ai, prod.sageox.ai) | PUBLIC Go binary; one bad ship lands on every SageOx user's machine |
| BYOK tokens | Server-side secrets in Secrets Manager | User-provided model API keys handled CLIENT-SIDE; leak vector is the user's machine |
| Auth surface | RequireRepoAccess / RequireTeamMember middleware | Mostly local commands; OAuth device flow for ox login; tokens cached locally |
| Untrusted input | Inbound from users (BFF -> api-go) | OUTBOUND PRODUCER of Ledger entries; ALSO consumes Ledger/Team-Context as untrusted input from other coworkers |
| Secrets handling | gitleaks pre-commit + CSI mounts | gitleaks-as-LIBRARY embedded for write-time + pre-push redaction (existing — internal/session/raw_writer.go + cmd/ox/prepush_scan.go) |
| MCP exposure | None | ox CLI hosts MCP servers; tool dispatch driven by LLM output |
| K8s / IaC | Heavy (Helm, Terraform, RDS, EKS) | None — single Go binary |

So the ox CLI pipeline reuses the ARCHITECTURE (6-phase Synthesia shape, Sonnet/Opus model split, perspective-framed hunters, dedup-before-validate) but swaps:
- Hunters: drop pii-boundary + authz (no api-go primitives); ADD token-handling, mcp-trust, ledger-write-redaction-bypass, local-fs
- IaC tooling: drop Checkov + Kubescape (no Helm/Terraform)
- Secret handling: EXTEND the existing gitleaks-as-library, do not bolt TruffleHog or anything else on
- Dashboard: reuse the SHARED Dependency-Track instance from monorepo (one DT serves both repos as separate projects)
- GH Action: similar shape but smaller — daily batch on sensitive-path diff, manual dispatch, label trigger

## Locked decisions (inherited from monorepo design)

- Never blocks merge.
- Three run modes: pre-commit fast tier (opt-in via SEC_PRECOMMIT=1), daily batch GH Action, on-demand /security-review or `make sec`.
- OSS stack: OpenGrep + govulncheck + OSV-Scanner + Syft+Grype. NOT Trivy (compromised twice March 2026). NOT TruffleHog (live verification can touch prod systems).
- Validator model split: Sonnet ~90%, Opus on authz / cryptography / multi-hop-taint / agent-tool-abuse / exploitability-dispute. (Token-handling and MCP-trust live in the agent-tool-abuse / exploitability classes for Opus routing.)
- Inline comments cite source articles for non-obvious tooling decisions (Synthesia post, Trivy advisories, OpenGrep fork rationale).

## Repo structure (mirror monorepo's pattern)

- .claude/skills/security-review/ (in-repo skill)
- security/ (committed config + threat model + custom rules + scripts)
- security/.output/ (gitignored runtime artifacts)
- .github/workflows/security-review.yml (thin trigger -> security/scripts/orchestrate.sh)
- bin/ (gitignored, populated by `make sec-install`)

## Cost (rough)

ox CLI has lower PR volume than monorepo (~10-15 PRs/week vs ~96/week). Daily batch typically skips on quiet days. Estimate: $1-2/day on the daily batch. On-demand runs free (subsidized Claude Code tokens).

## Out of scope for this epic

- Standing up a separate Dependency-Track instance (reuse monorepo's at https://dependency-track.tooling.sageox.ai with a new project_id for ox CLI).
- Anything K8s/Helm/Terraform-related (ox CLI has none).
- Provenance verification for releases (Cosign + SLSA on the published binary) — separate workstream that belongs to the release pipeline, not /security-review.

## Cross-reference

Sister epic: sageox/sageox-monorepo bead ox-557ft. Read that first for the full design rationale + shared decision log; this epic captures only the ox-CLI-specific deltas.

title: settings.json rewritten on every Claude Code session
description: MarshalSettings uses encoding/json defaults: SetEscapeHTML(true) escapes <, >, & in permissions; Unmarshal decodes \uXXXX to literal runes; MarshalIndent strips trailing newline and re-indents RawMessage values. Daemon autofix checkClaudeHooksFormat (every 30min) and ox doctor --fix compare canonical bytes byte-for-byte against on-disk, so any of those deltas trigger a rewrite forever. The existing idempotency test seeds {"hooks": {"PostToolUse": "echo legacy"}} — none of the drift-triggering bytes — so the test passes by tautology (round-trips encoder's own output). Fix: MarshalSettings uses Encoder.SetEscapeHTML(false), preserves trailing newline via a parameter from callers; both no-op guards switch to semantic equality (parse-then-parse) via a new SettingsSemanticallyEqual helper. Plan at /Users/ryan/.claude/plans/system-instruction-you-are-working-velvety-snowflake.md

title: Scope pre-push secret gate to sessions/ only
description: PR #597 added a pre-push secret gate (cmd/ox/prepush_scan.go) that scans ALL changed files in the push range, not just sessions/. This produces persistent false positives on legacy data/github/** PR/Issue cache files (PR titles/bodies containing strings matching aws_sts_session_key, generic_secret, etc.), blocking ox doctor's reconcile from succeeding. The internal/ledger.SetFieldRedactor chokepoint already protects data/github/** at write time, so re-scanning at push time is duplicative for new files and unrecoverable for legacy ones. Plus the recovery message points to ox session audit / ox session redact which only operate on sessions/.\n\nFix: scope scanPrePushForSecrets and scanAllTrackedFiles to paths under sessions/ only. Trust the writer-side chokepoint for everything else. Doctor's checkLedgerSecrets keeps visibility into legacy bytes (read-only).
close_reason: 0.8.1 ships scope-to-sessions + unwire data/github redactor; follow-up auto-redact-and-retry tracked in ox-y3ok

title: test(doctor): harden against network/git-push from doctor tests
description: cmd/ox/doctor_test.go and cmd/ox/doctor_display_test.go run runDoctorChecks against the real environment with no -short guard and no //go:build !short tag. Tests reach the daemon-discovered team context and shell out to real git push. Cascade-deadlocks the package via shared sync.Once on getCachedDoctorChecks. title: lfs.MutateSessionMeta is bypassed by 5+ direct WriteSessionMeta(Only) callers (concurrent-write race)
description:
lfs.SessionMeta gained an append-only Redactions field in ox-8bfh, persisted via MutateSessionMeta (flock + atomic rename). However, at least five pre-existing call sites perform read-modify-write on meta.json WITHOUT taking that lock and call WriteSessionMetaOnly / WriteSessionMeta directly:

- cmd/ox/session_push_summary.go:487-499 (Files update)
- cmd/ox/session_regenerate.go:606-725 (Files update)
- cmd/ox/session_upload_cmd.go:107,146-150 (Files update)
- cmd/ox/agent_session.go:1309-1329 (initial write + Files update)
- internal/daemon/agentwork/session_finalize.go:1437-1440 (unmarshal/modify/write)

Concurrent writers will lose updates — including Redactions entries written by 'ox session redact' between a racing reader's read and write. The risk is bounded today because redact-history runs are operator-initiated and the daemon typically doesn't run during them, but the invariant is fragile.

Fix: refactor each call site to use MutateSessionMeta(ctx, sessionDir, func(meta *SessionMeta) (*SessionMeta, error) { ... }), doing all reads + mutations inside the locked callback. Verify with a test that ledger-cache integration tests still pass; add a build-time grep to detect any new direct WriteSessionMeta(Only) caller (similar to make check-no-git-lfs-shell).
notes: Surfaced by CodeRabbit on PR #599 (review of ox-8bfh). The bypass paths predate this PR but the new Redactions field makes the consequences more visible — losing a redaction-pass record is worse than losing a Files entry because the audit trail goes silent.

title: ledger: meta.json files contain unresolved git merge conflict markers
description: At least 7 session meta.json files in the SageOx ox ledger have unresolved conflict markers committed (e.g. <<<<<<< Updated upstream, >>>>>>> Stashed changes around the summary_attempts field). Example: sessions/2026-02-13T14-56-ajit-OxmoZK/meta.json line 13. This blocks hydration entirely: lfs.ReadSessionMeta fails JSON parse, openSessionContent returns an error, the file becomes unscannable by the credential audit (~34 sessions in this ledger). Likely root cause: daemon's git pull --rebase --autostash path stashed local edits to meta.json (anti-entropy or summary regeneration), then a stash pop produced conflicts that were committed verbatim instead of being resolved. Fix: (1) audit ledger for files with conflict markers via ox doctor and offer auto-resolve (pick one side per a rule); (2) prevent the daemon write path from committing files containing <<<<<<<. .claude/rules/daemon-git.md says the daemon only reads/pulls — so the write that committed these came through the CLI or summary-regen path. Reproduce by inducing concurrent meta.json writes during a daemon pull cycle.
notes: Discovered while running ox session redact-history --dry-run on the SageOx ox ledger after ox-zukx fix landed; surfaced as 'parse session meta: invalid character <' from openSessionContent.

title: secrets: add dedicated github_pat detector (ghp_, gho_, ghs_, github_pat_)
description:
Today the only way 'ox doctor --check=ledger-secrets' catches a leaked GitHub Personal Access Token is via env_assignment (GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_...) or url_with_password (https://x-access-token:ghs_@github.com/...). A bare 'ghp_<36 chars>' string in tool output, error message, or pasted log — common in real sessions — has no detector.

Fix: add patterns to internal/session/secrets.go (or extra detectors) for:
  - ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}        (Keywords: ['ghp_'])
  - gho_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}        (Keywords: ['gho_'])
  - ghu_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}        (Keywords: ['ghu_'])
  - ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}        (Keywords: ['ghs_'])
  - ghr_[A-Za-z0-9]{76}        (Keywords: ['ghr_'])
  - github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{82} (Keywords: ['github_pat_'])

The 'ghp_' prefix is GitHub's official, documented, machine-detectable PAT shape. Every one of these is also documented by gitleaks; the project already pulls some gitleaks-derived detectors. Verify gitleaks_generated.go does not already cover these — if it does, just confirm Keywords are tight; if not, add hand-ported variants in gitleaks_detectors.go.

title: doctor/redact-history: ledger-secrets scan is broken in 3 ways
description:
Three structural bugs in the credential-scan flow used by 'ox doctor' and 'ox session redact-history':

1. SCOPE: scanLedgerForSecrets walks the entire ledger tree (incl. data/, root, .sageox/cache/ as a side effect of inverted skip list) instead of being scoped to session recordings. Surfaces 1428 'findings' inside data/github/.../pr/597-*.json (the PR about credential redaction containing example credentials).

2. HYDRATION: opens files directly with os.Open and reads pointer-file bytes for LFS-dehydrated sessions. On a real ledger with 153 stub sessions (115 with no cache), the scan silently treats them as 'scanned, clean' — completely missing whatever PATs are in those dehydrated session bytes. An external auditor found leaked git PATs that ox's tool did not surface; almost certainly due to this gap.

3. DETECTOR: internal/session/secrets.go:ScanForSecrets ignores the SecretPattern.Keywords pre-screen mechanism that the write-time chokepoint uses. heroku_key (a bare UUID regex with no Keywords guard) matches every UUIDv7 — 2141 false positives on this real ledger, against 0 real heroku tokens.

Fix scope: iterate <ledger>/sessions/<name>/ only; for each scannable file, route through cmd/ox/session_content.go:openSessionContent which auto-hydrates pointers to .sageox/cache/sessions/<name>/ via the LFS Batch API (NEVER in-place — see .claude/rules/cache-only-design.md). Update ScanForSecrets to lowercase input once and apply p.MatchesKeyword(lowerInput) before Pattern.MatchString. Add Keywords:['heroku'] to the heroku_key detector.
notes: Supersedes ox-50j5 (the heroku_key bug is one prong of this).

title: Consolidate raw.jsonl writes through session.RawWriter chokepoint + gitleaks detector integration
description: Today every raw.jsonl write site calls the redactor independently (6 call sites). Adding a new adapter or write path means remembering the discipline — the writePlanHistoryRaw and rewriteRawJSONL gaps were exactly this failure mode. Build session.RawWriter as the only public API to write raw.jsonl; embed cmd-allowlist redactor + builtin Redactor + gitleaks detector set. AGPL on TruffleHog rules it out as a library; gitleaks (MIT) gives 150 detectors at a faster scan rate.
close_reason: session.RawWriter chokepoint shipped. Single API (NewRawWriter, NewRawWriterTruncate, WriteEntry, WriteRaw) with three-layer redaction stack: CommandRedactor + builtin Redactor + gitleaks-derived extras (40+ new patterns including OpenAI, Anthropic, GCP, Datadog, Linear, Notion, Vault, Sentry, Discord, Slack webhook, Square, Shopify, Planetscale, etc.). All six prior write sites migrated: session_watcher.go, agent_hook.go:appendRedactedEntries, coworker.go:appendEntryToSession, agent_session_plan_history.go:writePlanHistoryRaw, session_regenerate.go:rewriteRawJSONL, session_redact_history.go:redactFileInPlace. Even ledger_twin test fixtures go through the same chokepoint. New make check-raw-writer-chokepoint target greps the source tree and fails the build if any file (outside raw_writer.go itself) calls os.OpenFile/Create/WriteFile against raw.jsonl directly. 14 chokepoint tests cover canary detection across all three layers, JSONL validity, append vs truncate, close-rejection, nil safety. Gitleaks rules ported as static data (MIT licensed); TruffleHog rejected due to AGPL-3.0 transitive licensing.

title: Forensic scrub of historical local Ledgers (per-finding human approval)
description:
## Problem

Forensic scan 2026-05-10 found historical credentials in already-committed local Ledger working trees:
- 16 committed sessions with AWS ASIA
- 2 with GitHub PAT
- 2 with share-session cookies
- 8 PR cache files with Bearer headers

Some are in unpushed local commits; future commits or rebases may move them around. Either way, they live in local git history until scrubbed.

## Fix

One-shot interactive tool: `ox session redact-history` (or similar). For each finding:
1. **Snapshot first** — copy the affected Ledger to an object-locked location (S3 with compliance mode, or local immutable backup). Print SHA-256 + path of the snapshot. Document chain of custody.
2. Present a redacted preview of the finding (type + file + line, never the secret value).
3. Ask: keep / redact-in-place / quarantine.
4. On redact-in-place: rewrite the affected file in the local working tree, amend the holding commit (NOT a history-rewrite of pushed commits — that's a separate v2 follow-up requiring customer comms).
5. Re-run scan, confirm finding count went to 0 for that finding ID.

## Constraints
- NEVER auto-approve. Per-finding human approval is the safety mechanism.
- NEVER push during this operation. Block push until scan returns clean.
- If a finding is already in a pushed commit, this task fails loud and points at the v2 git-history-rewrite follow-up.

## Acceptance
- Walkthrough: plant 1 canary in a committed file, run tool, redact-in-place, re-scan, finding gone, file is in expected redacted state.
- Snapshot bucket actually receives a copy.
close_reason: Implemented as 'ox session redact-history' in cmd/ox/session_redact_history.go. Workflow: scan via shared scanLedgerForSecrets primitive, classify by push status (refuses to operate on pushed commits — points at gated V2 rewrite), snapshot ledger to immutable tar.gz with SHA-256 BEFORE any modification, per-finding interactive prompt (no bulk-approve flag), atomic in-place redaction via temp+rename, git commit --amend on the holding commit, post-scan to report remaining findings. --dry-run lists without snapshotting/modifying. 5 tests cover snapshot determinism, in-place redaction, push-status classification, dry-run inertness, yes/no/quit interactive paths.

title: ox doctor: warn (and optionally auto-strip) .git/config files containing embedded GitLab PATs
description:
## Problem

Forensic scan 2026-05-10 found the GitLab PAT `glpat-…` embedded in `.git/config` of 9 local Ledgers — first leaked 2026-03-13. No doctor check today flags this.

## Fix

New doctor check: walk every local Ledger, run `extractPATFromRemote()` (already exists at `internal/gitserver/remote.go:133`), report repos with embedded PATs. With `--fix`, call `StripRemoteCredentials()` (already exists at `internal/gitserver/remote.go:197`) idempotently per repo.

Pair with the credential-helper fix (child task: stop-embedding-by-default) so the strip is durable rather than re-injected by the daemon on next sync.

## Acceptance
- `ox doctor --check=ledger-embedded-creds` flags each affected repo.
- `ox doctor --check=ledger-embedded-creds --fix` strips creds idempotently.
- After fix, `git remote -v` shows bare URLs; `git fetch` still works (credential helper resolves auth).
close_reason: Implemented as part of doctor_ledger_secrets.go; --check=ledger-embedded-creds detects oauth2:TOKEN@ in origin and --fix calls gitserver.MigrateLedgerCredentials (the same primitive the daemon startup sweep uses).

title: ox doctor: scan local Ledgers for unredacted credentials (read-only report)
description:
## Problem

There's no first-class way to ask the ox CLI "do my local Ledgers contain any credentials right now?" Today the user has to run ad-hoc grep across `~/.local/share/sageox/sageox.ai/ledgers/`. Forensic scan 2026-05-10 found multiple credential classes in 12 GB of local Ledger data; the user had no built-in surface to detect this until a third party (me) ran grep against it.

## Fix

Add a doctor check (`cmd/ox/doctor_*.go` family) that:
1. Walks every local Ledger working tree (skip `.git/`, `.dolt/`, `.beads/`, `.bak`, `.gc-cache`).
2. Runs the `DefaultPatterns` set from `internal/session/secrets.go` against every `*.jsonl`, `*.json`, `*.md`, `*.txt`, `*.vtt`.
3. Prints a SUMMARY table: detector_name, count, distinct values, first/last session timestamp, repo affected.
4. **Does NOT print secret values.** Truncates to type + length + first-N prefix chars.
5. **Does NOT upload findings.** Local-only. Local-only. Local-only.

## Acceptance
- `ox doctor --check=ledger-secrets` returns a structured report.
- `ox doctor --check=ledger-secrets --json` machine-readable.
- Exit code reflects severity: 0 = clean, 1 = findings, 2 = scan error.
- Documented in `cmd/ox/release_notes.md`.
close_reason: Implemented checkLedgerSecrets in cmd/ox/doctor_ledger_secrets.go and registered as --check=ledger-secrets. Also implements --check=ledger-embedded-creds (ox-yeae) which strips embedded PAT via gitserver.MigrateLedgerCredentials on --fix. Read-only, local-only, never prints matched bytes.

title: Whole-output redaction for trusted credential-emitting commands (aws sso, gh auth, glab auth)
description:
## Problem

Some commands emit credentials in shapes that don't match a single regex line — `aws sso login` prints multi-line ASCII output with embedded ASIA + secret + session token; `aws configure export-credentials` emits AWS env-export blocks. Relying on per-regex matching leaves edge cases.

Forensic scan found 14 distinct AWS ASIA tokens across 16 sessions, all from `aws sso login` or related shell output captured into `tool_result` events.

## Fix

Maintain a `command_allowlist_redaction` map (cmd-prefix → redaction policy). For known credential-emitting commands, redact the ENTIRE `stdout` of the matching tool_result event with a placeholder like `[REDACTED:credential-output:aws-sso-login]`. The regex detectors stay as defense-in-depth, but whole-output redaction is the primary boundary.

Suggested entries:
- `aws sso login` → whole-output redact
- `aws sts assume-role` → whole-output redact
- `aws configure export-credentials` → whole-output redact
- `aws sts get-session-token` → whole-output redact
- `gh auth login` → whole-output redact
- `gh auth token` → whole-output redact
- `glab auth login` → whole-output redact
- `glab auth token` → whole-output redact
- `vault read auth/...` → whole-output redact
- `op item get` (1Password CLI) → whole-output redact

## Acceptance
- Synthetic integration test: simulate `aws sso login` shell output as a tool_result; assert recorded raw.jsonl contains the placeholder, no token chars present.
- Allowlist documented; adding a new entry is a 1-line change.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bug: daemon session_finalize never commits LFS pointer rewrite after push
description: The daemon's ProcessResult in session_finalize.go:1117-1124 calls WritePointerFiles after a successful push, but NEVER commits and pushes the pointer rewrite. The CLI path (agent_session.go:1361) calls commitPointerRewriteAndPush which does a second git add/commit/push. Without this second commit, the remote ledger has raw blobs alongside meta.json claiming storage=lfs. The web frontend (api-go) reads meta.json, sees LFS, calls FetchSmallLFSContent with the OID, and fails because the git tree has the raw blob not a pointer. 8 sessions currently affected (all from May 1-5). Fix: add a call to commitPointerRewriteAndPush (from cmd/ox/session_upload.go:195) or equivalent in the daemon's ProcessResult after WritePointerFiles succeeds.
