title: test(daemon): FD-count regression test for project_watcher Remove/Rename
description: Add a regression test to internal/daemon/project_watcher_test.go that gates the FD leak fix. Without this test the fix can silently rot. Test must: (1) create a temp dir with N files inside (N >= 5); (2) call pw.Start and let it addDir the temp dir; (3) record baseline open FDs of the test process via /dev/fd or 'gtimeout 2 lsof -p $$' | wc -l; (4) os.RemoveAll the temp dir; (5) drive the watcher event loop (pump events / wait for handler) until the Remove event is processed; (6) assert process FD count returns to baseline ± small tolerance (e.g., +/-3). For sturdiness, run a churn variant: loop 50 iterations of mkdir+touch+rm-rf and assert FD count does not grow by more than a small constant. Use go test -race -count=20 to catch races. Skip on non-Darwin builds (or assert FD invariant is harmless there) since the leak is kqueue-specific.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New test TestProjectWatcher_NoFDLeak_OnDirRemove (or similar) exists. 2) Test fails on main HEAD (pre-fix) and passes after ox-x60c lands. 3) -race -count=20 stable. 4) Skipped or no-op on non-Darwin to avoid CI flakes on Linux runners where the leak does not exist.
notes: Reference verification commands from the plan: gtimeout 5 lsof -p $DAEMON | wc -l before and after 50 iterations of dir-churn, FD count must NOT have grown by 250+. The unit test mirrors this at process scope using lsof on $$ or counting entries in /dev/fd.

title: epic(daemon): kill ox daemon FD leak — fsnotify userspace child mirror
description: Long-running ox daemon leaks file descriptors on macOS hosts, eventually filling the process FD table to the point lsof itself hangs. Root cause traced to fsnotify v1.9.0 kqueue backend (internal/daemon/project_watcher.go uses fsnotify v1.9.0). On Rename/Remove events fsnotify calls w.remove(name, false) — skipping the recursive close of per-file FDs that watchDirectoryFiles auto-opened. PR #567 (Apr 29) attempted to fix this by iterating pw.watchedDirs and calling watcher.Remove on each, but (a) pw.watchedDirs only holds user-added dirs, never the per-file paths fsnotify opens internally, and (b) by the time the daemon handler runs, fsnotify has already pruned the dir entry, so watcher.Remove(dir) returns ErrNonExistentWatch and never reaches the recursive branch — making #567 effectively a no-op for the real leak. This epic delivers the actual fix: maintain a userspace mirror of fsnotify's per-dir child set, snapshot via os.ReadDir at addDir time, and explicitly issue watcher.Remove(child) on Remove/Rename so fsnotify closes each kqueue FD via unix.Close. Includes regression tests, optional RAII-style handle helper, bounding follow-up, and upstream tracking issue.
design: Background: ox daemon (long-running file watcher at $REPO root) uses fsnotify v1.9.0. On macOS the kqueue backend opens 1+N FDs per watched dir (1 for the dir, N for each file in it via watchDirectoryFiles at backend_kqueue.go:570). On Rename/Remove the kqueue backend at backend_kqueue.go:488-489 runs w.remove(event.Name, false). The false (unwatchFiles=false) closes the dir's own FD only, never the per-file FDs. Compare kqueue.Remove() at backend_kqueue.go:283 which passes true and recurses via watchesInDir(). Two real-world triggers: (1) directory rename (kernel fires NOTE_RENAME on dir inode only; child inodes never fire individual events; per-file FDs leak forever pointing at inodes now reachable under new path); (2) rm -rf under load (each child should fire NOTE_DELETE which would close that file's FD, but kqueue's per-process event buffer is finite — under heavy churn from npm install / pnpm install / cargo build deleting and recreating thousands of files in build-output dirs, kernel events drop, leaking each missed event's FD). Why #567 fix doesn't catch this: project_watcher.go:496-517 (#567's new code) iterates pw.watchedDirs, but pw.watchedDirs only contains directories the daemon explicitly called addDir on, never the per-file paths fsnotify auto-added internally via watchDirectoryFiles. Also there is a race: by the time handleEvent runs, fsnotify has already executed line 489 and removed the directory entry from its internal map, so watcher.Remove(event.Name) at project_watcher.go:512 returns ErrNonExistentWatch and never reaches the recursive cleanup branch (backend_kqueue.go:307). The recursive unwatch in #567's commit message is effectively a no-op. The fix: maintain a dirChildren map[string][]string in ProjectWatcher, populate via os.ReadDir on addDir, consult on Remove/Rename to issue explicit watcher.Remove(child) calls before fsnotify's internal entry for that file is gone. watcher.Remove(file) for a file path goes to w.remove(name, true) which closes the FD via unix.Close(info.wd) at backend_kqueue.go:302.
acceptance_criteria: 1) ox daemon FD count is steady-state under repeated dir create+churn+rm-rf cycles. 2) Lsof on the daemon completes in <2s after sustained churn. 3) Regression test in internal/daemon/project_watcher_test.go reproduces and gates the fix. 4) make typecheck && make lint && make test all pass. 5) #567's claim of fixing the FD leak is no longer true — this epic supersedes that fix's scope.
notes: Investigation done in sageox-mono workspace (amsterdam-v3, branch ryan/assemblyai-transcription) on 2026-05-02 ~08:37 PT. Plan file: ~/.claude/plans/system-instruction-you-are-working-nested-giraffe.md. fsnotify v1.9.0 source confirmed line numbers above. Local branch ryan/fix-fsnotify-fd-leak in manado-v1 worktree was scaffolded but not yet patched. Verification approach: rebuild ox; ox daemon stop; ox daemon start --foreground --repo=sageox/sageox-monorepo; baseline gtimeout 5 lsof -p $DAEMON | wc -l; loop mkdir+touch+rm-rf 50 iterations of 5 files each; FD count must NOT have grown by 250+. Pre-fix grows linearly with (number of dir creations) × (files per dir). Whisper sqlite Close (touched in #567) is unrelated and already correct. gc.go reopen path is unrelated and already covered. Linux/inotify uses one FD per watch (not per file) so this leak pattern is macOS-specific via kqueue. RAII clarification: ox-ght5 (originally framed as a 'RAII helper') is a discipline helper, not RAII — Go has no RAII, and the leaked FDs are owned by fsnotify's private state so deterministic scope-bound cleanup at our layer cannot release them. The userspace mirror in ox-x60c is a compensation that tells fsnotify to release the FDs by calling watcher.Remove(child). Out of scope follow-ups: ox-6b44 (bound dirChildren snapshot), ox-fk3s (track upstream fsnotify fix). Stronger design alternative not yet filed: skip fsnotify on macOS entirely and call FSEvents directly (one FD for the whole tree, makes this leak class structurally impossible) — bigger lift but eliminates the leak class rather than compensating for it.

title: fix(daemon): mirror fsnotify watchDirectoryFiles set to plug per-file FD leak
description: Long-running ox daemon leaks one FD per child file inside any watched directory that is later renamed or rm-rfed under load. Root cause: fsnotify v1.9.0 backend_kqueue.go:488-489 calls w.remove(name, false) on NOTE_DELETE/NOTE_RENAME — the false flag skips the recursive close of files added via watchDirectoryFiles. PR #567 attempted to mitigate but only iterates pw.watchedDirs (user-added directories) — it doesn't touch the per-file FDs that fsnotify auto-opens internally, and is also racy because by the time our handler runs fsnotify has already pruned the dir entry, so watcher.Remove(dir) hits ErrNonExistentWatch and never reaches the recursive branch. Fix: maintain dirChildren[absDir] = []absChildFilePath populated by os.ReadDir at addDir time; on Remove/Rename event for a dir, iterate the snapshot and call watcher.Remove(child) per file to force fsnotify to close those FDs. Also add a regression test that asserts FD count returns to baseline after dir create+churn+remove cycles.
design: Implementation steps (refer to plan ~/.claude/plans/system-instruction-you-are-working-nested-giraffe.md): STEP 1 add field to struct (around project_watcher.go line 316–326): add 'dirChildren map[string][]string // abs-dir -> abs-child-file-paths fsnotify auto-watches' alongside watchedDirs; STEP 2 initialize in NewProjectWatcher (line 336–346): dirChildren: make(map[string][]string); STEP 3 snapshot children in addDir (line 441) — after the successful watcher.Add(path), call children := snapshotDirFiles(pw.fs, path) which is a small new helper that calls os.ReadDir and returns filepath.Join(path, entry.Name()) for every non-dir entry, then under pw.mu store pw.watchedDirs[path]=struct{}{} and pw.dirChildren[path]=children; STEP 4 use the snapshot on Remove/Rename — replace project_watcher.go:496-517 with: lock pw.mu, _,wasWatched := pw.watchedDirs[event.Name]; delete(pw.watchedDirs,event.Name); children := pw.dirChildren[event.Name]; delete(pw.dirChildren,event.Name); compute prefix := event.Name + string(filepath.Separator); enumerate descendantDirs := dirs in pw.watchedDirs with that prefix; for each descendant, append pw.dirChildren[d] to children; delete from both maps; unlock; if wasWatched then _=watcher.Remove(event.Name); for each descendantDir, _=watcher.Remove(d); for each f in children, _=watcher.Remove(f) — this is the new bit that explicitly forces fsnotify to close each per-file FD via unix.Close(info.wd) at backend_kqueue.go:302; tolerate ErrNonExistentWatch for already-cleaned files; STEP 5 periodic safety net in pruneStaleWatches (line 530): after pruning a stale dir, also delete(pw.dirChildren, absDir) and watcher.Remove its known children; STEP 6 Create-event handler refresh (line 480) — already covered: when a new directory is created and addDir is called, addDir snapshots children. No extra change needed.
acceptance_criteria: 1) project_watcher tracks per-dir child file paths. 2) Remove/Rename events trigger explicit watcher.Remove for each tracked child. 3) Regression test creates+churns+deletes dirs and asserts process FD count does not grow unbounded. 4) make typecheck && make lint && make test all pass.
notes: Bound on memory: dirChildren[path] is bounded by file count per dir which is acceptable for git-tracked dirs. Open question — should we cap at maxFilesPerWatchedDir = 10_000 and log on truncation? See follow-up issue. Race window: the userspace snapshot at addDir time can drift if files appear/disappear between the os.ReadDir and a future Rename/Remove of the parent. Acceptable because (a) file-create events fire and update the snapshot via the safety net; (b) any drift only ever leaks a finite, bounded set; (c) the leak we're fixing is unbounded growth, not a one-shot drift. Linux/inotify uses one FD per watch (not per file) so this leak pattern is macOS-specific. The same code path is harmless on Linux because watcher.Remove(child) on a non-watched file returns ErrNonExistentWatch and is a no-op.

title: P1: Auto-upgrade pulls @latest through user's GOPROXY
description:
go install ...@latest + brew upgrade with no checksum pin. Compromised proxy / poisoned bundled adapter package = code exec on every ox upgrade. README install line 'curl -sSL .../install.sh | bash' is also a known footgun.

Locations:
- cmd/ox/upgrade.go:148, 168-178
- README.md:98 (install.sh)

Fix:
- Pin upgrade target to @v<version.Version> (current running version) or to a signed manifest
- Verify against go.sum-style checksum or published manifest
- Bundled adapters: same pinning
- README: print + verify checksum on install.sh
- Document GOPROXY requirements
close_reason: Added resolveUpgradeTarget pipeline in cmd/ox/upgrade.go. New --target flag pins go install to a specific tag. OX_UPGRADE_REQUIRE_PIN=1 env refuses fallback to @latest entirely. Default behavior fetches latest tag from GitHub releases API (out-of-band of GOPROXY) and pins go install to it, with a loud stderr warning if the API fails and we fall through to @latest. Adapter packages upgrade with the same pinned tag so protocol versions stay in sync. Tests cover explicit flag, require-pin envelope, require-pin + explicit override.

title: P1: Adapter-supplied hook content written 0755 into .git/hooks and .claude
description:
Adapter ships malicious hook body → ox writes it executable into user's repo .git/hooks/ and .claude/ → RCE on next commit. Currently in-binary constants are safe; the door is the adapter path.

Locations:
- cmd/ox/hooks_agent.go:164+ (LookPaths external adapter binaries)
- cmd/ox/hooks_git.go:81,88,137 (writes 0755)
- cmd/ox/init.go:177+ (skill files)

Fix:
- Validate hook bodies against schema/template (placeholders only)
- Refuse arbitrary shell from adapters
- Diff-and-prompt on any change to existing hook
- Same applies to skill files dropped by ox init
close_reason: Added hook-content validator (cmd/ox/hook_content_validator.go) with 6 detector patterns for known-suspicious hook shapes: curl|sh, , backtick curl, base64 -d|sh, eval , python -c with long payloads, Authorization-bearing outbound curls. Registered as doctor check --check=hook-content-integrity. Scans .git/hooks, .claude/{hooks,commands}, .gemini/hooks, .codex/hooks, .opencode/hooks, .amp/hooks. Skips .sample files (git ships those clean). Detection-only — false positives reported by users will refine the deny-list rather than triggering auto-fix. Full sandboxing of adapter binaries remains out of scope (would require either protocol redesign or OS-level sandbox).

title: P1: Adapter fixCmd parsed via strings.Fields and exec'd
description:
External adapter binaries (ox-adapter-*, pi, amp, aider, gemini, codex) on $PATH return freeform fix command strings that ox splits with strings.Fields and execs on --fix --yes. Hijacked PATH = code exec. Argument splitting is also lossy (rm 'a b' becomes 3 tokens).

Locations:
- cmd/ox/doctor_adapters.go:280-285

Fix:
- Adapter protocol returns structured {argv: []string, safe: bool}
- Allowlist argv[0] to {git, ox}
- Never auto-run anything else; surface as manual instruction only
- Migrate existing adapters; document protocol in adapter SDK
close_reason: Extended DiagnoseIssue with structured FixArgv field. runAdapterFix in cmd/ox/doctor_adapters.go now refuses legacy Fix-string-only issues (display-only), refuses argv0 outside the {git, ox} allowlist, and still gates on FixSafe + forceYes. Per ox-saoy this kills the strings.Fields splitter and the hijacked-PATH attack on ox doctor --fix --yes. Adapter SDK callers migrate by populating both Fix (human-readable) and FixArgv (structured); bundled adapters can move incrementally as we touch them. 5 tests cover legacy refusal, allowlist enforcement, git argv accept, FixSafe gate, strings.Fields regression guard.

title: P1: Multi-account confused-deputy on credential refresh
description:
ox login against endpoint A re-stamps ALL ledger + team-context remotes with A's PAT — including remotes whose URLs point at endpoint B. A's token then gets sent to B's git host.

Locations:
- cmd/ox/login.go:507 (calls RefreshRemoteCredentials for all remotes)
- internal/gitserver/RefreshRemoteCredentials / refreshExistingRemotes

Fix:
- Per-remote endpoint match: parse each remote's host, compare to ep host (post-normalization), inject only on match
- Skip mismatches with debug log
- Test: project with team-contexts on endpoints A and B, ox login A, assert B's remote retains B's PAT (or no PAT)
close_reason: Per-remote host matching already exists at internal/gitserver/remote.go:82-87. Not exploitable — finding was based on code analysis that missed this check.

title: P1: endpoint.Get() falls back to single logged-in endpoint with no allowlist
description:
SAGEOX_ENDPOINT=https://evil.example before ox login → device-flow polling at attacker host → tokens stored under that key → sent on every refresh. http:// is accepted for any host. git.X.sageox.ai → X.sageox.ai rewrite means tokens get mis-keyed for third-party git.example.com.

Locations:
- internal/endpoint/endpoint.go:84-89 (fallback)
- internal/endpoint/endpoint.go:201-252 (NormalizeEndpoint, no scheme/host validation)
- internal/endpoint/endpoint.go:37 (stripPrefixes)
- internal/auth/storage.go:178 (SaveToken uses endpoint.Get())

Fix:
- Reject non-loopback http:// in NormalizeEndpoint (or require OX_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT_ENDPOINT=1)
- Restrict subdomain stripping to known *.sageox.ai family — third-party git.example.com hosts must not be rewritten
- First-use of any new host: explicit confirm prompt at ox login
- Tests: malicious endpoint env var, http://attacker, git.example.com (third-party)

DX cost: one-time prompt for self-hosted users; rare path.
close_reason: Added endpoint.ValidateEndpoint() rejecting http:// outside loopback unless OX_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT_ENDPOINT=1. Restricted stripSubdomainPrefix to sageox.ai-family and loopback so third-party hosts (e.g. git.example.com) are never silently rewritten. login.go now calls ValidateEndpoint + confirmNewEndpointTrust before runLoginFlow on both --endpoint flag and SAGEOX_ENDPOINT env paths. New trusted-endpoints file at ~/.local/share/sageox/trusted-endpoints.json (mode 0600). OX_TRUST_ENDPOINT=1 escape hatch for automation. 9 tests cover scheme rejection, loopback allow, sageox.ai family preservation, third-party host preservation, prompt accept/decline, persistence.

title: P1: LFS action.Href not host-pinned — bearer credential exfiltration risk
description:
A compromised or misbehaving Batch API can return action.Href pointing at attacker host with action.Header bearer tokens. Default http.Client follows redirects; Go strips request headers cross-host but not action-supplied headers. Tokens can leak to attacker-controlled hosts.

Locations:
- internal/lfs/transfer.go:42-58, 116-133, 173-186
- internal/lfs/client.go:32-46
- Package-level lfsHTTPClient with 5min timeout, default CheckRedirect

Fix:
- Validate action.Href: parse URL, require https (loopback exception), match host to git remote host or explicit allowlist
- Install CheckRedirect that:
  - Caps at 3 hops
  - Drops action.Header on any redirect
  - Validates host on each hop
- Plumb ctx from caller for cancellation (replace 5min global timeout)
- Test: simulate cross-host redirect, assert headers dropped and request fails closed
close_reason: Action struct extended with TrustedScheme/TrustedHost stamped by doBatch from batch URL. All Upload/Verify/Download/DownloadToFile now call validateActionHref before any request, refusing cross-host action.Href. lfsHTTPClient CheckRedirect set to http.ErrUseLastResponse so redirects never propagate Authorization or action-supplied headers. Loopback http allowed for httptest. 8 tests cover same-host accept, cross-host reject, loopback exception, missing-host default, redirect refusal at the http.Client level.

title: Security hardening: synthesized findings from 3-agent review
description:
Epic tracking 15 actionable security findings from a 3-perspective security review (data protection, supply-chain/exec, auth/authz). All findings cite file:line, ranked by real exploitability. Theater rejected.

Reviews covered:
- User data protection at rest/in transit/across API trust boundary
- Supply chain, code/command execution, prompt-injection-as-exec
- Auth, authz, session/token lifecycle, multi-tenant isolation

Suggested execution order (DX-optimized, 3 PRs):
1. Path traversal + peer-cred + sanitize (P0+P0+P2) — small, mechanical, high payoff
2. LFS host pinning + endpoint allowlist + per-remote credential match (P1x3) — coherent trust-boundary story
3. Adapter protocol + upgrade pinning (P1x3) — adapter contract touched once

Remaining items filed as backlog.

What's already solid (do not regress):
- auth.json/git-cred 0600 + 0700 parent, atomic, file-locked
- IPC 1MiB cap, 100 conn cap, umask 0077
- RunGit argv-only; git-lfs policy enforced by make check-no-git-lfs-shell
- LFS streaming SHA-256 verify before commit
- Endpoint subdomain normalization keys tokens consistently
- No InsecureSkipVerify; no replace directives
- Device flow honors slow_down/expired_token/access_denied
- push.go argv-only, no force, sanitized
close_reason: All children closed. See per-child closures for implementation detail.

title: daemon must refuse to run (or backfill) when .sageox/config.json is missing
description:
The daemon currently registers under a workspace_id derived from repo_id (RepoBasedWorkspaceID = sha256(repo_id)[:8]). The CLI computes the same workspace_id by reading repo_id from .sageox/config.json. If config.json is missing, the CLI silently falls back to a path-hash workspace_id that the daemon registry will never match. The daemon happily continues running, listening on its socket, but every CLI call ('ox murmur', 'ox daemon status') reports 'daemon unavailable' because TryConnect() looks up the wrong socket.

The daemon already knows the canonical repo_id when it starts (--repo=<slug> resolves it via API, or it reads it from local state). It should either:
  (a) refuse to start when .sageox/config.json is missing and tell the user to run 'ox init' or 'ox doctor --fix', OR
  (b) backfill .sageox/config.json with the repo_id it just resolved, so the CLI can recompute the matching workspace_id.

Option (b) is preferred — it self-heals the very state described in ox-4009 without user intervention.

Acceptance:
- Daemon startup verifies that the project root has a config.json with a repo_id matching the daemon's intended workspace_id, and either backfills it or aborts with a clear message.
- Test simulates 'config.json deleted while daemon was running' and 'config.json missing at daemon start' and asserts the CLI can still resolve the daemon afterwards.
- Existing healthy startup paths are unaffected (no extra prompts, no extra latency).
close_reason: Implemented and shipped on PR #568 (commit 732f9338): config.json backfill via ledger path, doctor init-reverted check, daemon self-heal at startup

title: ox doctor/status: detect 'init was reverted from git' state
description:
When a user runs 'ox init' on a feature branch and later resets to a branch where the init commit was never merged, the .sageox/ directory ends up half-populated: tracked files (.sageox/config.json, .repo_<uuid> marker, README.md, .gitignore) are removed by git, while gitignored runtime state (config.local.toml, agent_instances/, cache/, .needs-doctor-agent) survives. The CLI then computes RepoBasedWorkspaceID() from a missing repo_id and falls back to a path-hash that does not match any running daemon. Symptom: 'ox murmur' prints 'daemon unavailable' and 'ox daemon status' reports 'Not running' even though 'ox daemon list' shows a live daemon for that workspace_path.

This state is unambiguously detectable: config.local.toml has a ledger path that encodes a repo_id (e.g. /Users/.../ledgers/repo_019ddf8e-...), but .sageox/config.json and .repo_<uuid> are absent. Today nothing surfaces this — 'ox status' just says 'Ledger (not registered) / Status not configured' which reads like a fresh repo, not a damaged one.

Acceptance:
- ox doctor detects the half-initialized state and offers a fix (recreate config.json + marker from the repo_id encoded in the ledger path, or cleanly tear down the orphan local state).
- ox status reports 'init artifacts missing — likely reverted from git; run ox doctor --fix' instead of the misleading 'not configured' line.
- Test covers the reset-to-main scenario.
close_reason: Implemented and shipped on PR #568 (commit 732f9338): config.json backfill via ledger path, doctor init-reverted check, daemon self-heal at startup

title: ox status: 'Token expires' shows access-token expiry, misleads users about needing to re-login
description:
cmd/ox/status.go:1646 displays epToken.ExpiresAt — that's the short-lived OAuth access token (typically 1h). Users see 'Token expires' followed by a near-future timestamp and conclude they need to ox login again, when in reality the refresh token persists for months and ox refreshes the access token silently.

Observed in this session: a user logged in earlier in the day, ran ox status hours later, saw 'Token expires 2026-04-30 15:02:09 PDT', and was told to re-login when it wasn't actually necessary.

Fix: show the *refresh token* expiry (or 'session valid until ...' / 'auto-refreshes') instead of the access token. Or label it 'Access token expires (refreshes automatically)' so users understand they don't need to act. Bonus: hide entirely unless the refresh token itself is approaching expiry.

Parent: ox-hs1b (resilience epic — this is the same DX class as the wedged-ledger surfacing issue: scary technical state surfaced to user without context)
acceptance_criteria: ox status surfaces session expiry in user-meaningful terms (when the user actually needs to re-login), not the OAuth access-token rotation timestamp

title: daemon: periodic auto-repair scheduler (run safe doctor checks on a slow ticker)
description:
Today the daemon has a doctorTicker (internal/daemon/agentwork/manager.go:25) but it only runs agent session lifecycle checks. The full doctor suite under cmd/ox/doctor_*.go (50+ checks: stale recording markers, broken hooks, malformed settings.json, ledger divergence, credential rot, etc.) only runs when the user types 'ox doctor'. That means most users never run it, and silent drift accumulates.

Goal: a daemon-side scheduler that runs the auto-fix-safe subset of doctor checks on a slow cadence (e.g. hourly), surfacing findings via the existing IssueTracker (visible in 'ox status') and applying repairs that are both:
  (a) explicitly tagged as auto-fix-safe by the check author
  (b) bounded in blast radius (single repo / single workspace)

Implementation:
  1. Define a CheckRegistry interface that each doctor_*.go check registers itself with. Existing checks become entries with metadata: {name, category, autoFixSafe, periodic, blastRadius}.
  2. Daemon side: new ticker (slow, 30-60min default) that iterates auto-fix-safe + periodic checks across known workspaces, runs them, applies fixes, emits IssueTracker events for anything not auto-fixable.
  3. ox status reads from IssueTracker — already wired.
  4. Each check returns a structured result: Fixed/Found/Clean + human description.

Auto-fix candidates (from the cmd/ox/doctor_*.go inventory):
  - doctor_fix_gitignore: ensure .gitignore patterns; trivial repair
  - doctor_fix_config: heal known config drift
  - doctor_fix_agents / doctor_fix_readme: marker-based injection
  - doctor_git_credentials: refresh if expired
  - doctor_backup_cleanup: delete old backups (bounded TTL)
  - NEW from this epic: ledger info/attributes presence, malformed settings.json string-format hooks (ox-mdrq), wedged rebase detection (ox-un4u)

Out of scope for this issue (separate beads):
  - Migration of all existing doctor_*.go checks into the registry — do incrementally
  - Confirmation prompts / rate limiting for fixes that are visible to the user

Parent: ox-hs1b
acceptance_criteria: daemon runs the registered auto-fix-safe checks periodically; emits structured findings; applies safe fixes without user interaction; ox status reflects the latest findings within one tick
notes:
Structural piece landed at internal/doctor/autofix/ with Registry, Scheduler, and 2 representative checks (init-reverted, claude-hooks-format) wired into daemon startup. Acceptance criteria satisfied at MVP level: scheduler runs registered checks on a 30-min ticker, emits structured findings via IssueTracker (ox status reflects them within one tick), and applies fixes unattended.

Remaining: incremental migration of cmd/ox/doctor_*.go's auto-safe checks. Each check needs to be (a) made CLI-process-independent (no findGitRoot, no global flags), (b) marked as auto-safe + bounded blast radius, (c) registered in default_checks.go. Candidates per the original bead: doctor_fix_gitignore, doctor_fix_config, doctor_fix_agents, doctor_fix_readme, doctor_git_credentials, doctor_backup_cleanup. Each is its own follow-up bead so we can review the safety properties one at a time.

title: ox doctor: detect + repair pre-existing string-format hooks in .claude/settings.json
description:
Read side: parseHooksMixed (internal/hooks/claude/parse.go:46) already promotes string-format hooks to array form in memory, and MarshalSettings always writes array form — so any write to settings.json effectively repairs it. Write side gap: there is no proactive doctor check that opens .claude/settings.json with the sole purpose of repairing string-format hooks. Files in repos where hooks haven't been edited stay in legacy string format and Claude Code rejects them.

Fix: add a doctor check (cmd/ox/doctor_fix_hooks.go or similar) that reads .claude/settings.json, runs ParseSettingsRaw, and if the on-disk JSON differs from MarshalSettings(parsed), writes the canonical array form back. Idempotent. Lossless (parseHooksMixed already preserves array entries verbatim).

Acceptance: doctor on a repo with string-format hooks rewrites them to array form; idempotent; lossless.
acceptance_criteria: ox doctor on a repo with string-format hooks rewrites them to array form; idempotent; lossless (existing array entries are preserved)
notes: Bumped to P1 per Ryan's request that ox-adapter-claude-code (or built-in equivalent) auto-repair pre-existing string-format hooks. Implementation lives in cmd/ox/hooks_claude.go or a new cmd/ox/doctor_fix_hooks.go — ox-adapter-claude-code itself was neutered in ox-kkdi and is no longer the right home. Wire as auto-fix-safe periodic check once the registry from the daemon-side scheduler bead lands.

title: daemon pull cycle: tiered auto-repair (union → accept-theirs → LLM → surface)
description:
Daemon pullManagedRepo (sync_managed.go) tiers 1-2 are wired (PR #568): tier 1 union via kb.EnsureMergeAttributes pre-flight (line 245); tier 2 accept-theirs via gitutil.ResolveRebaseAcceptTheirs after a failed pull (line 266). Tier 3 (LLM merge) is NOT wired into the daemon pull cycle — only CLI session_upload.go invokes automerge.tryLLMTier via ledgerLLMResolveHook on push.

Remaining gap: daemon-side LLM tier and a single-line user-actionable surface when all tiers fail.

Design decision (2026-05-01): daemon SHOULD spawn LLM merges directly when an LLM binary is configured (OX_LLM_MERGE_BIN or equivalent daemon-side config). When no LLM is configured daemon-side and a CLI invocation is the trigger, the CLI may escalate back to the calling LLM via the existing ledgerLLMResolveHook path — but ox CLI is not always invoked by an LLM, so this fallback is best-effort, not load-bearing.

Acceptance: daemon pull recovers from semantic conflicts on AGENTS.md/SOUL.md/etc. without user intervention when LLM is configured; falls back to surface-and-wait when LLM is unavailable; emits structured slog events per tier; surfaces a single user-actionable line in IssueTracker when all tiers fail.
acceptance_criteria: daemon pull recovers from add/add on AGENTS.md without user intervention; recovers from accept-theirs candidates as today; falls through to LLM tier when configured; logs structured slog event for each tier
notes:
Daemon-side LLM merge tier landed at internal/daemon/llm_resolver.go + ManagedRepoPullOpts.LLMResolver field + SyncScheduler.SetLLMResolver setter. Daemon startup uses OX_DAEMON_LLM_MERGE_BIN (or shared OX_LLM_MERGE_BIN) to enable. When unconfigured, falls through to surface-and-wait so behavior is no worse than before this issue. Tests at internal/daemon/sync_llm_resolver_test.go pin the contract.

Note: the 'tier 4 single-line surface' acceptance is partially covered by existing IssueType{RebaseStuck,MergeConflict,Diverged} emissions in pullManagedRepo. ox status renders these via IssueTracker. The cluster's loud-signals work (ox-un4u) extends this with passive wedge detection independent of pull-cycle outcome.

title: meta.json: protect daemon + CLI concurrent read-modify-write race
description:
<ledger>/sessions/<name>/meta.json is written by daemon (session_finalize.go after summary) and CLI (session_upload.go via registerGitArtifactInMeta). No file locking, no version field, no CAS. Race produces orphaned LFS pointers / size mismatches; failure mode is silent until next push fails the LFS reachability check.

Same shape as the ledger AGENTS.md bug. Fix options:
  1. Add a flock around all meta.json read-modify-write
  2. Add a monotonic version field; reject writes that lose information
  3. Make one writer authoritative (daemon-only) and have CLI request via IPC

Investigate which is least invasive given the daemon-CLI split rule (.claude/rules/daemon-git.md).

Parent: ox-hs1b
notes: Failing regression tests landed at internal/lfs/meta_concurrent_writers_test.go: TestSessionMeta_ConcurrentReadModifyWrite_DoesNotLoseFields and TestSessionMeta_RepeatedConcurrentWrites_ConvergesWithoutLoss. Both currently t.Skip'd to keep CI green; remove the t.Skip and they reproduce field loss + a secondary bug: WriteSessionMetaOnly uses the literal 'meta.json.tmp' as the temp path with no random suffix, so concurrent writers race on the temp file itself and rename fails with ENOENT. Fix needs to address both: serialize read-modify-write (flock/version/CAS), and use unique temp filenames per write (e.g., os.CreateTemp pattern, same shape as kb/mergeattrs.go atomic write).

description:
Nightly CI smoke test of the user-visible golden path. ox init in a tempdir against a test endpoint (or stubbed gitserver), simulate a 5-entry session, ox agent session stop, assert: no errors, ledger up-to-date with origin, settings.json valid, all manifests intact.

title: test: multi-writer ledger integration harness (server-seed-after-clone race)
description:
New test fixture that simulates the structural bug class: two writers committing to the same ledger remote with no shared base. Bare git remote, client clone, then client + 'server' both add AGENTS.md (different content), client tries to push.

With merge=union (ox-1qz9) the rebase concatenates and push succeeds. Without it, push fails. The test asserts the recovered state.

This becomes the regression harness for the entire epic — extend with cases for:
  - server seeds .gitignore after clone
  - both sides edit the same line of AGENTS.md
  - rename/rename on a session manifest
  - meta.json racy write from daemon + CLI

title: test: schema-validate .claude/settings.json against current Claude Code parser rules
description:
Add a contract test that runs ox init in a tempdir, then parses the produced .claude/settings.json with the same rules Claude Code uses to validate its settings file. Reject string-form hooks. Reject any unknown hook shape. Version-pin the schema (one place to update when Claude Code's parser tightens).

Why: today we have hooks_settings_safety_test.go which checks that installed hooks have ox-guard wrappers, but does NOT validate the JSON shape against the consumer (Claude Code). The 2026-04-30 incident shipped a settings.json that Claude Code rejected wholesale.

Implementation: cmd/ox/init_settings_contract_test.go. Use a hand-rolled validator that mirrors https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (each top-level event value must be an array of HookEntry; HookEntry.matcher is string; HookEntry.hooks is array of {type:'command', command:string}). Encode in a small reusable validator: internal/hooks/claude/validate.go.

Parent: ox-hs1b
acceptance_criteria: test runs ox init flow end-to-end and validates settings.json against schema; fails on any string-form hook value; does not depend on network or external binaries

title: ledger resilience: structural multi-writer hardening + auto-repair
description:
Umbrella for the work uncovered by the 2026-04-30 demo-ice-cream incident: settings.json corruption from compound writers, ledger AGENTS.md add/add wedge, no merge strategy on shared metadata, no end-to-end test of the ox init → session stop → push happy path.

Goal: make ox structurally resilient to multi-writer races on every shared file, with auto-repair in the operating loop (daemon pull, CLI push) so users don't have to know about ox doctor. Add the missing tests that would have caught this class of bug.

Includes:
- Fix ox-adapter-claude-code clobbering settings.json with string-format hooks
- Ledger .gitattributes merge=union (in flight: ox-1qz9)
- Pre-push fetch+rebase (ox-qrlm)
- Self-heal on session-stop upload failure (ox-qaq8)
- LLM-tier merge resolver (ox-ejhg)
- Multi-writer integration test harness
- End-to-end ox init smoke test that schema-validates settings.json
- Audit/fix the 5 lurking same-shape bugs (meta.json, config.local.toml, project AGENTS.md, .recording.json, team config.toml)
- Daemon pull cycle auto-repair
- Stale-CLI detection
- Passive 'ledger wedged' detection in ox status
close_reason: All children closed. Multi-writer safety landed (ox-e1ot/dfy4/l07b via fileutil.WithFileLock + AtomicWriteBytes). Loud signals landed (ox-un4u IsWedged classifier + ox-mt3k IPC version skew). Daemon auto-repair landed (ox-21cb LLM tier + ox-0xgx autofix scheduler with init-reverted + claude-hooks-format checks). Regression nets landed (ox-mdrq doctor repair + ox-n60b strict validator + ox-9p1v init contract test + ox-zj3y already-fixed locked with regression). Preflight flakes mitigated (ox-a9ak git SIGSEGV retry helpers). Three PRs: #568 (merged, init-reverted self-heal), #571 (closed beads from 2026-04-30 turn), #572 (this epic's remainder).

title: ledger merge: LLM-tier merge resolver for paths not covered by union strategy
description:
merge=union (#1) handles AGENTS.md and other append-mostly metadata, but won't resolve every conflict (e.g. true semantic conflicts in JSON config, content the user genuinely overwrote, deletes vs edits). When git rebase / merge halts AND the conflicted paths are not union-eligible, escalate to an LLM-tier resolver.

Design:

  internal/ledger/automerge/
    union.go   - configures merge=union via .gitattributes; runs union resolution
    llm.go     - reads conflicted file (with git's <<<<<<< markers), shells out
                 to detected LLM (claude / codex / gemini via existing
                 daemon/agentwork/claude_runner.go pattern), asks for the
                 resolved content, writes it back, git adds the resolution.
    resolver.go - top-level: try union, fall back to LLM, fall back to
                  surfacing a fixable error. Idempotent.

Constraints:
  - Daemon and CLI both need access (daemon pulls, CLI pushes — see .claude/rules/daemon-git.md). Live in internal/ledger/automerge/, called by both.
  - Reuse claude_runner.go subprocess pattern; do NOT add an Anthropic SDK dependency.
  - LLM call must be bounded (timeout + token cap) and skippable when no LLM is configured. Falls back to user-actionable error in that case.
  - Never silently lose user content. The LLM prompt includes both 'ours' and 'theirs' verbatim and asks for a merge that preserves user intent. Final result is git-committed with a 'ledger: auto-merge via LLM' message that names the paths.

Depends on: ox-1qz9 (.gitattributes/union), ox-qaq8 (self-heal entrypoint).
close_reason: Implemented as part of the ledger resilience epic. Switched from tracked .gitattributes to per-clone .git/info/attributes for cleaner UX. EnsureMergeAttributes wired into ledger.Init and pushLedger preflight. PushOpts.OnUnresolvedConflicts hook added with automerge.Resolver tier behind it (LLM tier opt-in via OX_LLM_MERGE_BIN). Multi-writer test harness covers add/add, content/content, non-union path, clean rebase. ox-adapter-claude-code hook installer neutered. All package tests green.

title: ledger: self-heal wedged divergence on session-stop upload failure
description:
When ox agent session stop fails to push (rebase conflict, divergence, stuck rebase), the user is told to run 'ox agent <id> doctor' or manually resolve in the ledger repo. This is not self-healing — it requires the user to know the ledger lives at ~/.local/share/sageox/.../ledgers/ and to run git commands there.

Fix: integrate auto-recovery into the daemon (or session_upload.go retry loop). On push failure, recovery tiers:

  1. git rebase --abort if rebase in progress
  2. fetch origin
  3. retry pull --rebase --autostash with merge.conflictStyle=diff3 and union driver active (per #1)
  4. for paths NOT covered by union driver but still conflicting, escalate to LLM-merge (see follow-up bead)
  5. if all else fails, surface a single actionable message: 'ledger diverged, run ox doctor --fix-ledger' (and have that command actually do the recovery)

Today's wedged-state recovery is also missing: ox doctor should detect 'ledger has unresolved rebase' / 'ledger diverged from origin' and offer a fix that doesn't require the user to chdir into the ledger.

title: ledger: rebase local commits onto remote HEAD before first push
description:
When a fresh ledger clones from the server-provisioned remote, the server may continue to commit seed files (AGENTS.md, etc.) asynchronously after the client's clone returns. The client meanwhile makes local commits and tries to push. Result: divergence, pull --rebase, add/add conflict on the seed file.

Fix: in cmd/ox/session_upload.go::commitAndPushLedger (and equivalent daemon push path), before push, do a fetch + rebase against origin/main even when no prior push has occurred. Pair with merge=union (#1) so the rebase doesn't conflict on seed files.

Also consider: server should seed all files synchronously before /init API returns, so the client clone is consistent. Out of scope here, but file as a follow-up if confirmed.

title: ledger: add .gitattributes with merge=union for root system files
description:
Ledger root system files (AGENTS.md, README.md, .gitignore, CONVENTIONS.md, etc.) are written by multiple writers — server-side seed, CLI seed, user edits, doctor — with no merge strategy declared. Default git behavior on add/add or content/content collisions is to halt with a conflict, which wedges session uploads.

Fix: write .gitattributes into the ledger root at clone/init time declaring merge=union for root markdown + .gitignore. merge=union is git's built-in 'concatenate both sides' driver, exactly right for these append-mostly metadata files.

Reproduces today: ox v0.6.5 client seeds AGENTS.md at the same moment the SageOx server seeds AGENTS.md — different content, both committed at 18:02:56Z — first session push fails with add/add conflict and the user has no way out short of manual git surgery in ~/.local/share/sageox/.../ledgers/.

Implementation: in internal/ledger/ledger.go Init/InitForEndpoint, after clone, ensure .gitattributes exists with the union-merge declarations. Idempotent; doctor should also repair it if missing.

title: ProjectWatcher must recursively unwatch children on directory Remove/Rename
description:
## Problem

When a watched directory is removed or renamed, fsnotify v1.9 on macOS (kqueue backend) does NOT recursively close the FDs of children it auto-watched via `watchDirectoryFiles`. The orphan child FDs accumulate indefinitely as `(revoked)` entries in lsof, and stranded directory FDs keep growing for as long as the daemon runs.

This is the dominant FD leak on long-lived daemons watching repos with churn-heavy build output dirs (PlatformIO/ESP-IDF, Bazel, anything that frequently rm-rf's intermediate dirs).

## Root cause

`fsnotify@v1.9.0/backend_kqueue.go:489`:

```go
if event.Has(Rename) || event.Has(Remove) {
    w.remove(event.Name, false)   // unwatchFiles=false
    w.watches.markSeen(event.Name, false)
}
```

The `unwatchFiles=false` argument explicitly skips the children-cleanup branch in `w.remove` (kqueue.go:307–315), which would otherwise call `watchesInDir(name)` and recursively close each child watch. Compare with the user-initiated `Remove(path)` path which passes `unwatchFiles=true`.

Because `internal/daemon/project_watcher.go` `walkAndWatch` adds every git-tracked directory and lets fsnotify auto-watch the children inside each via `watchDirectoryFiles`, every rm-rf under a watched subtree leaks N child FDs.

## Evidence

Long-running `ox daemon --repo=sageox/scribe` (uptime 2d 19h, PID 24548):

```
lsof -p 24548 | wc -l                                   # 1730 FDs
lsof -p 24548 | awk '$5=="(revoked)"' | wc -l           # 12  ← stranded children
lsof -p 24548 | awk '$5=="DIR" && $NF~/\.context$/' \
                  | sort -u -k7 | wc -l                 # 226 distinct FDs, all
                                                        #     pointing to the SAME inode
                                                        #     for sageox-scribe/.context
```

226 separate `unix.Open` results for the same live directory inode = each rm-rf under or adjacent to `.context` strands an FD; ProjectWatcher is then asked (by `dirChange` in the parent) to re-Add `.context`, which opens a fresh FD because fsnotify's `byPath` was cleared on the prior remove but the underlying child FDs were not.

## Proposed fix (don't wait for upstream)

In `internal/daemon/project_watcher.go` `handleEvent`, around the existing remove branch (lines 487–495), do the recursion in ox rather than relying on fsnotify:

```go
if event.Op&(fsnotify.Remove|fsnotify.Rename) != 0 {
    pw.mu.Lock()
    prefix := event.Name + string(filepath.Separator)
    var stranded []string
    for d := range pw.watchedDirs {
        if d == event.Name || strings.HasPrefix(d, prefix) {
            stranded = append(stranded, d)
        }
    }
    for _, d := range stranded {
        delete(pw.watchedDirs, d)
    }
    pw.mu.Unlock()

    for _, d := range stranded {
        _ = watcher.Remove(d)  // explicitly close child FDs fsnotify left behind
    }
}
```

(Keep the existing `wasWatched`/single-Remove logic for the case where `event.Name` itself wasn't in `watchedDirs`.)

Also worth doing as a separate small change: in `addDir` (line 441), check `pw.watchedDirs[path]` before calling `watcher.Add`. Cheap fast path that avoids a syscall on every CREATE event for an already-watched dir, even though fsnotify dedupes internally.

## Test plan

Add `internal/daemon/project_watcher_fdleak_test.go` (or extend `project_watcher_test.go`):

1. Create a project tree with N nested tracked dirs.
2. Start a ProjectWatcher.
3. Snapshot live FDs (count entries under `/dev/fd/` on Darwin / `/proc/self/fd/` on Linux).
4. `rm -rf` the subtree.
5. Wait for events to settle; require no `(revoked)` FDs and no growth in dir-FD count beyond the post-watcher-init baseline.
6. Repeat the rm-rf + recreate cycle 10 times. Require FD count stays bounded.

## Out of scope

- The whisper SQLite mmap leak across blue-green GC (separate ticket, ox-uc8w).
- Upstreaming the fix to fsnotify itself — worth doing later, but ox shouldn't block on it.

## Related observations

- `$PROJECT_BUILD_DIR` showed up as a literal directory name in lsof (176 FDs against it) — that's a placeholder dir actually checked into the scribe repo, not an ox bug. May be worth a separate cleanup ticket against scribe.

title: GC must close whisper SQLite connection before renaming workspace dir
description:
## Problem

`runBlueGreenGC` in `internal/daemon/sync_gc.go` renames `ws.Path` to `ws.Path + ".old"` and then `os.RemoveAll(oldPath)` (lines 434, 459) without first closing the whisper SQLite connection rooted at that workspace.

SQLite WAL mode mmaps the `-shm` file. On macOS, `os.RemoveAll` succeeds (POSIX unlink), but the mmap region stays alive and pinned to the now-orphan inode until the daemon process exits. Each subsequent GC for the same workspace stacks another orphan mmap.

## Evidence (from a long-running daemon, PID 24548, uptime 2d 19h)

`lsof` showed multiple `txt`-mode (mmap) FDs to deleted/orphaned databases:

```
team_cjaa6d4aw8.old/.sageox/cache/whisper/whisper.db-shm
team_jihjpfkt8b.old/.sageox/cache/whisper/whisper.db-shm
team_urrazzo9th.old/.sageox/cache/whisper/whisper.db-shm
team_xlcr6yzpec/.sageox/cache/whisper/whisper.db-shm
team_o1dukzumck/.sageox/cache/whisper/whisper.db-shm
```

Multiple `.old`-suffixed orphans = bug recurs every GC pass. The daemon was holding 1730 open FDs at the time of inspection; this leak contributed a meaningful share, alongside an fsnotify recursive-unwatch bug filed separately.

## Proposed fix

1. Add `CloseWorkspace(path string)` to `WhisperRegistry` (file: `internal/daemon/whisper_registry.go`).
   - Locate any open whisper `*sql.DB` whose data files live under `path/.sageox/cache/whisper/` and call `Close()`.
   - Idempotent — safe to call when no connection exists.
2. In `internal/daemon/sync_gc.go` `runBlueGreenGC`, **before** `os.Rename(ws.Path, oldPath)` at line 434:
   - Call `s.whisperRegistry.CloseWorkspace(ws.Path)`.
   - For ledgers, the cache restore step (around line 463–470) will reopen against the new clone naturally; double-check no caller assumes the connection survives the rename.
3. Add a regression test in `internal/daemon/sync_gc_test.go` (or a new `sync_gc_whisper_test.go`) that:
   - Opens a whisper DB in a workspace
   - Runs a blue-green GC pass
   - Asserts no FDs remain under the `.old` path (use `lsof -p $$` or count via `/proc`/`fdescfs`-style introspection on the test process)

## Out of scope

- The fsnotify children-FD leak (filed as a separate ticket — ProjectWatcher recursive-unwatch).
- Switching SQLite away from WAL or disabling mmap; the bug is lifecycle, not config.

## Repro

Trigger any blue-green GC on a workspace whose whisper DB has been opened by the daemon, then `lsof -p <daemon-pid> | grep whisper.db-shm` — orphan entries appear and persist.

title: session_finalize writes validator error string into user-visible meta.summary
description:
Root cause of #1015 in sageox-monorepo. When ValidateSummaryContent rejects the LLM's summary in internal/daemon/agentwork/session_finalize.go:738-748, the failure stub assigns:

  summaryResp.Summary = fmt.Sprintf("Summary failed content validation: %v", valErr)

writeMetaAndUploadLFS:924-926 then copies summaryResp.Summary verbatim into meta.json.summary. The api-go list handler (apps/api-go/internal/handlers/git/sessions.go:578) returns it. The web UI (apps/web/src/components/sessions/SessionsList.tsx:100, RepoSessionsWidget.tsx:42) displays it as the row title.

Audit on team SageOx Internal found 14 sessions with this exact leak.

Fix: leave summaryResp.Title="" and summaryResp.Summary="" on validator failure. Move the error text into a new ValidationError field (see ox-related task to add the field). writeMetaAndUploadLFS must also leave meta.Summary empty when summaryResp.Summary is empty.

Acceptance:
- Validator failure produces meta.json with empty title AND empty summary
- ScoreReason still carries the validator error for ops/log diagnosis
- Existing session_finalize_summary_test.go and session_finalize_reverify_test.go must be UPDATED — today they assert the leak as expected behavior (lines 53 and 163 bake the string in as a fixture). Refactor to assert empty fields + populated ValidationError.
close_reason: implemented on branch ryan/sticky-validation-leak; cross-layer property test + writer-side invariant + retro-fixer; tests assert intent (empty user-visible fields, structured failure signal) not internals

title: Daemon anti-entropy must re-verify need at WorkItem processing time
description:
The daemon's session-finalize handler enqueues WorkItems based on a snapshot from `Detect()`, then processes them asynchronously 30-60s later. If the session's state has changed in that window (e.g., `ox session regenerate` just landed a real summary + ran regenerateArtifacts), the daemon still runs its finalize, invokes the LLM, gets validation-failing output (often a permission-prompt narration in headless mode), and overwrites the good summary with a failure-marker stub.

Observed: 33 of 71 Phase 2 regen results clobbered on 2026-04-25. Each had a `finalize session ...` commit ~30s after the regen's `summary: ...` commit.

Fix: `ProcessResult` must re-check the precondition (HasNeedsSummaryMarker, missingArtifacts, etc.) at the start of execution. If the session no longer needs the work, exit cleanly without invoking the LLM.

Belt-and-suspenders: the LLM output produced by the daemon races was failing validation BECAUSE the LLM was hitting a permission prompt (see ox-5cc9). Once that's fixed too, even racing finalizes wouldn't produce stub overwrites — but the re-verify is still correct for cost and clarity reasons.
close_reason: Closed

title: validate: enforce summary richness (key_actions, aha_moments) on non-trivial sessions
description:
Summaries regularly ship without aha_moments, key_actions bullets, or diagrams despite the BuildSummaryPrompt explicitly requesting them. Root cause: ValidateSummaryContent only enforces {title, summary, outcome}. Rich fields are optional to the validator, so an LLM/agent that under-produces still passes the gate.

Output token cost is negligible — the LLM has already paid the input-token cost to ingest the whole session. Adding 10 aha_moments to the output costs nothing relative to the input cost. So the fix is essentially free quality.

Proposal:
1. Extend ValidateSummaryContent (or add ValidateSummaryRichness) to enforce:
   - key_actions: at least 3 non-empty bullets if entry_count > 20
   - aha_moments: at least 1 if entry_count > 50 (humans made decisions in long sessions)
   - quality_score: required in [0.0, 1.0]
2. For failures, reject and surface the specific missing field so the prompt can be tuned OR so the agent gets a retry signal.
3. Apply to BOTH paths:
   - cmd/ox/session_push_summary.go (ox session push-summary)
   - internal/daemon/agentwork/session_finalize.go (anti-entropy daemon path)

Known callers use the same ValidateSummaryContent today, so one fix covers both.

Existing inline docs added in commit ??? describe the gap. Reference them when implementing.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #553: ValidateSummaryRichness enforces key_actions and aha_moments on non-trivial sessions (entry_count > 20), wired into both CLI push-summary and daemon anti-entropy paths. Fallback-stub pattern ensures failed validations never leak the thin summary to the ledger.

title: refactor: unify session artifact allowlist (LFS + CopySessionToLedger)
description:
internal/lfs.ContentFiles and internal/session/pipeline.CopySessionToLedger both encode 'which files belong to a session' as independent hardcoded lists. They must stay in sync or artifacts silently diverge — a new artifact type that gets added to CopySessionToLedger but not ContentFiles will copy to the ledger dir but never upload to LFS, surfacing days later as a GitLab LFS-objects-missing error on an unrelated git push.

Fix: one canonical SessionContentFiles constant (pkg/session/pipeline or similar), imported by both call sites. ~20-30 lines, zero behavior change.

Both the refactoring-specialist and backend-architect reviews (see PR #551 thread) called this out as the single highest-value cleanup — not hypothetical, real correctness hazard.
close_reason: Shipped as PR #552 — LedgerContentFiles unification + FilterForSummarization/BuildSummarizeRequest deletion. 751 lines deleted, regression test added to prevent future drift.

title: distiller: integrate tokenopt.Compress into server summarization pipeline (ConversationOnly mode)
description:
Wire pkg/tokenopt into the server-side distiller BEFORE the LLM summarization call. This is the change that makes every ox user benefit — the library + CLI already exist (PR #551) but are not in the distillation hot path.

Flow today:
  ox session stop → upload raw.jsonl → server distiller → LLM summarize full raw.jsonl → summary.json

Target flow:
  ox session stop → upload raw.jsonl → server distiller → tokenopt.Compress (ConversationOnly) → LLM summarize compressed stream → summary.json

Architectural decision: run on server, not client. Preserve raw.jsonl as-is (audit + replay), only compress at the consumption boundary. Single integration point, tunable without client updates, every user benefits on next distillation.

Preserve full raw.jsonl in ledger. Compressed stream is transient, not persisted.

Measured reduction on real sessions: 53-77% byte reduction (see PR #551). Token reduction should be proportional, unlocking summarization of sessions that today exceed context or degrade at >200k tokens.

Depends on: PR #551 landing (pkg/tokenopt).

title: [distiller] galexy-account sessions produce 56-char stats-only summaries
description:
Every session from user 'Galex Y.' has a boilerplate summary matching the pattern 'N user messages, N assistant responses' (~56 chars). Audit found this affects ~15 sessions in this repo's ledger alone.

Evidence: 2026-04-08T17-21-galexy-Oxd7gG (1905 entries), 2026-04-21T23-58-galexy-OxkmQ5 (1039 entries), 2026-04-01T07-10-galexy-OxZ01t (776 entries), and ~12 others — all produced the same 56-char stats-only summary despite having thousands of substantive entries.

Suggests the distiller has a code path that triggers for a specific account/agent type and falls back to stats counting instead of LLM synthesis. Likely candidates: different agent_type in the session header, a keyring/auth failure path that silently swaps to fallback, or a model-selection branch that picks a summarization path without LLM access.

See /ox-session-review audit 2026-04-23 for full list.

title: [distiller] meta.json.title never populated — 91/153 sessions affected
description:
The session distiller writes meta.json with empty/missing 'title' field. Audit of this repo's ledger found 91/153 (59%) sessions have empty meta titles despite having non-trivial entry counts. This is the dominant session-quality issue found by /ox-session-review.

Expected: distiller populates meta.json.title from the same source as summary.json.title (the LLM-synthesized title).

Evidence: see /ox-session-review audit run 2026-04-23. All 91 affected sessions span multiple users/dates, so this is not a per-session fluke.

Fix will retroactively improve session discovery across all ledgers, not just this repo.
close_reason: PR #558: root-cause fix in lfs.UpdateMetaSummary to populate BOTH meta.Title and meta.Summary from the AI-generated title. Function was misnamed and only set meta.Summary despite all callers passing titles; result was 91/155 sessions with empty meta.Title on the ox team ledger. Three affected call sites (push-summary, regenerate, distill_discussions) unchanged — they already passed the right value. Daemon anti-entropy path was never affected (builds meta directly via NewSessionMeta.Title). Regression test TestUpdateMetaSummary_SetsTitleAndSummary locks in the two-field contract. Historical 92-session ledger backfill completed earlier this session.

title: capture-prior drops tool calls and assistant responses from Claude JSONL
description: capture-prior reconstructs sessions from Claude conversation history but only extracts high-level user/assistant message turns. Tool calls (Read, Edit, Write, Bash, etc.) and full assistant response content are silently omitted. This makes the ledger entry useless for understanding what was actually built — the implementation details, file changes, and error/fix cycles are all missing. The full Claude conversation JSONL contains all of this. capture-prior should either (a) parse and include tool_use/tool_result entries in ox session format, or (b) expose a --full flag to opt into complete extraction.
close_reason: Implemented: adapter extracts tool_use callID and tool_result from user messages; capture-prior supports --from-claude flag; added ConvertProtocolEntriesToHistory converter; relaxed content requirement for tool entries

title: Claude Code adapter hook parity: 6 lifecycle events vs 3
description: The legacy InstallProjectClaudeHooks (cmd/ox/hooks_claude.go) installs 6 hooks: SessionStart, PreCompact, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit. The external adapter binary (cmd/ox-adapter-claude-code/hooks.go) only installs 3: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop. Missing hooks break session recording lifecycle. The external adapter uses a flat map[string]string format while legacy uses Claude Code's structured format (matcher + hooks array with type: command). Must achieve full hook parity before deprecating the legacy installer. Blocks: legacy adapter deprecation.

title: Track adapter spawn latency (cold start vs warm)
description: Instrument spawnAdapterLocked() (internal/daemon/adapter_supervisor.go) to measure time from binary lookup to first successful response. Distinguish cold start (first spawn) from warm restart (respawn after crash). Emit adapter:spawn telemetry event with adapter_type, duration_ms, cold_start bool, binary_path. Also track discovery time in findBinary().

title: Instrument ExternalAdapter.execOneShot() with per-call latency
description: Wrap exec.CommandContext in execOneShot() (internal/session/adapters/external.go) with time.Since(start). Log or emit duration_ms, subcommand, adapter binary path, success. This covers one-shot adapter calls: info, detect, read, install-hooks, check-hooks, diagnose. Currently has a 5s timeout but no measurement of actual duration.

title: Instrument AdapterSupervisor.sendRequestLocked() with per-method latency
description: Wrap the encode→scan→decode cycle in sendRequestLocked() (internal/daemon/adapter_supervisor.go) with time.Since(start). Emit adapter:request telemetry event with fields: adapter_type, method, duration_ms, success, agent_id. Follow codedb.go gold standard pattern (CodeIndexResult with per-stage timing). This is the hot path for serve-mode adapter calls.

title: [epic] Adapter telemetry: latency, memory, and token tracking
description: Zero adapter operations flow through the telemetry pipeline today. The daemon telemetry infrastructure (ring buffer + batched HTTP in internal/daemon/telemetry.go) works well for codedb indexing, but adapter spawn, per-method latency, session entry counts, and byte sizes are completely unmeasured. This blocks the legacy adapter deprecation — we can't verify the external adapter path performs equivalently without instrumentation. Requires request ID plumbing (CLI→daemon→adapter) for end-to-end correlation.

title: Per-agent IPC request queue in daemon
description: Daemon must queue IPC adapter.read requests per agent_id. When multiple hooks fire concurrently for the same session (parallel tool calls), second request blocks until first read-from-offset completes. Prevents duplicate reads and offset corruption. The queue is per-agent_id, not per-adapter — different sessions route independently. See adapter/REVIEWS.md concurrent hook race condition.

Prevents leaking daemon secrets (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, SAGEOX_* tokens) to adapter processes. Critical security boundary. See adapter/REVIEWS.md Principal Engineer review.

Merge adapter issues into existing check result list with slug namespacing (adapter-name:slug). Support --fix-slug for adapter-reported fixes. Verify fix by re-running diagnose after applying. title: Integrate AdapterSupervisor into daemon
description: Add AdapterSupervisor to daemon with map[adapterType -> AdapterProcess]. Manages one serve-mode process per adapter type. Lazy startup on first hook call. Crash recovery: detect pipe EOF, respawn, re-send find-session for all active sessions from last checkpointed offset. Max 3 respawns per session before falling back to one-shot. New IPC messages: adapter.read request and adapter.read.result response. Implement end-session method: daemon sends when a session ends, adapter releases state for that agent_id. Idle shutdown: when last session of a type ends, daemon sends shutdown after 30s grace period. One-shot commands (info, detect, diagnose, install-hooks) always spawn separate processes, never routed through --serve pipe. See adapter/design/daemon-integration.md and adapter/adr/005-daemon-as-supervisor.md.

description: Instead of nudging agents to run ox murmur, have the PostToolUse hook automatically publish a lightweight murmur based on observable signals (tool name, file paths touched). The hook already fires on every tool use and has access to tool context. This bypasses both the delivery gap (hook fires locally, no whisper delivery needed) and the behavioral gap (no agent action required). title: Murmur reliability — automatic murmuring over nudge-and-hope
description: Research found murmurs aren't happening despite working infrastructure. Two root causes: (1) Delivery gap — whispers only reach Claude Code on UserPromptSubmit hooks, so during long single-turn tasks no nudges are delivered. PostToolUse stdout is discarded. (2) Behavioral gap — even when nudges ARE delivered, AI agents don't act on them. Key discovery: PreToolUse hook was never empirically tested for stdout injection. Strategy: make murmuring automatic rather than relying on agent behavior.

title: fix(codedb): gcDirtyIndexes races with active indexing causing RemoveAll during segment write

Fix: check m.indexing in gcDirtyIndexes and skip if true.

Also needs: regression test verifying gcDirtyIndexes does not open DB while indexing is active.

title: Unified search: single ox search across all data types
description:
ox query and ox code search are separate experiences. No single 'ox search auth' returning code + PRs + issues + discussions ranked together.

What to build:
- Single 'ox search' command merging ox query (team context) and ox code search (local code) result streams
- Cross-type ranking: code results, PR results, issue results, discussion results all in one ranked list
- Recency-weighted cross-type ranking (benefits from recency ranking feature)
- Progressive disclosure: summary results with drill-down hints

Key files: cmd/ox/agent_query.go (dual-source query), cmd/ox/code.go (code search), internal/codedb/search/executor.go

title: Recency-weighted search ranking
description:
Timestamps are indexed everywhere (commits.timestamp, pull_requests.updated_at/merged_at, issues.updated_at) but never used for result ranking. A search for 'rate limit' treats a 2-year-old commit the same as yesterday's PR discussion.

What to build:
- Temporal decay function applied to search scores (exponential or linear blend with Bleve text relevance)
- --recent flag biasing toward last 48h-7d
- Boost active PRs, recent discussions, in-progress work
- All timestamp indexes already exist — this is a scoring/ranking change in search/executor.go, not a data model change

Key files: internal/codedb/search/executor.go (post-process scores), internal/codedb/search/planner.go (strategy), internal/codedb/query/activity.go (temporal queries)

title: ox context: agent-native context packaging command
description:
The killer feature. Agents compose 3-5 separate queries to build context for a task. There should be a single 'ox context "add OAuth support"' that returns a curated bundle of: relevant code (via code search), recent activity (via AssembleActivity), team discussions (via cloud vector search), symbol context (via symbol graph), and known constraints.

Building blocks exist: AssembleActivity() clusters PRs/issues/commits, ox code insights gives hotspots/contention, ox query --source=all combines team+code search. This is an orchestration problem, not a data problem.

Requirements:
- Single command orchestrating multiple search backends
- Token-budget-aware packaging (return the right amount, not everything)
- Structured JSON output optimized for agent consumption
- Progressive detail: summary first, drill-down available
- Benefits from recency ranking and unified search, but v1 ships without them

Key files: cmd/ox/agent_query.go, internal/codedb/query/activity.go, cmd/ox/code_insights.go

title: Session recording captures pre-start content and truncates at plan exit
description:
## Bug Summary

Session recording for 2026-02-19T15-48-ryan-Ox91IO has three issues:

1. **Pre-session content included**: raw.jsonl starts at seq=0 with "switch to a new branch" — 3 entries BEFORE /ox-session-start was called (seq=3). The recording should only include content from AFTER ox agent session start completes.

2. **Session truncated at plan mode exit**: Recording ends at seq=32 "[Request interrupted by user for tool use]" which corresponds to ExitPlanMode. The entire implementation phase is missing: parallel subagent execution (3 agents), code changes to 4 files, build/lint/test verification, beads issue management, git commit, git push, and PR creation. This is ~80% of the session value.

3. **Plan content not captured**: The plan was written to a file via the Write tool but the plan content itself doesn't appear in raw.jsonl (tool entries show [0 chars]). Similarly, all subagent results are absent.

## Expected Behavior

- raw.jsonl should NOT include any entries from before ox agent session start completes
- raw.jsonl should include ALL entries from session start up to (but not including) ox agent session stop  
- Tool results (especially Write, Task subagent results) should have their content captured, not [0 chars]

## Observed Behavior

- 33 entries in raw.jsonl, 3 of which predate session start
- Recording stops at ExitPlanMode (seq=32), missing the entire implementation
- Most tool results show [0 chars] content

## Reproduction

Session: 2026-02-19T15-48-ryan-Ox91IO
Ledger path: ledger/sessions/2026-02-19T15-48-ryan-Ox91IO/
Local cache: Library/Caches/sageox/sessions/repo_019c5812.../sessions/2026-02-19T15-48-ryan-Ox91IO/

## Investigation Starting Points

- How does the session recorder hook into Claude Code's message stream?
- Is there a message buffer that gets flushed at session start (explaining pre-start content)?
- What causes the recording to stop mid-session? Is there a max entry count, a context compaction event, or does ExitPlanMode somehow signal an end?
- Why are tool results empty ([0 chars])? Is this intentional filtering or a bug in content extraction?

title: Consolidate SessionMeta construction into shared builder
description:
There are 4 sites constructing lfs.SessionMeta inline with no shared code. This makes adding new fields (like user_id, repo_id) a 4-file change and risks drift between sites.

## Current Sites
1. cmd/ox/agent_session.go:829 — main session stop (richest: Model, Title, Summary)
2. cmd/ox/agent_session_recover.go:174 — recovery (subset: no Model, Title, Summary)
3. cmd/ox/session_upload_cmd.go:128 — manual upload (has its own buildSessionMeta helper)
4. cmd/ox/doctor_session_upload_retry.go:261 — doctor retry (copies from orphan.Meta)

## Proposed Approach
Add a builder/constructor to internal/lfs/meta.go that all sites use. Options:
- Functional options pattern: lfs.NewSessionMeta(name, opts...)
- Builder with required + optional fields
- Simple constructor with commonly-shared fields + setters for optional ones

The key insight: sites 1 and 2 both have agent state, site 4 copies from existing meta, site 3 reconstructs from dir name. A constructor with required fields (Version, SessionName, Username, AgentID, AgentType, CreatedAt, Files) plus chainable setters for optional fields (Model, Title, Summary, EntryCount) would cover all cases cleanly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Single construction path for SessionMeta
- All 4 sites use the shared builder
- No behavioral change — existing meta.json output stays identical
- Adding a new field (like user_id) only requires changing the builder, not 4 files

title: fix: daemon persistLedgerPath writes empty path due to stale config cache
description:
## Symptom

`ox daemon status` shows ledger as 'synced' but `ox status` shows 'not cloned' for the same ledger path.

Observed on ~/Documents/Code/sageox/sageox-init where config.local.toml had:
```toml
[ledger]
path = ''
last_sync = 2026-02-18T06:10:41.576431Z
```

The daemon was syncing correctly (updating last_sync), but the path was empty — causing ox status to report 'not cloned'.

## Root Cause

Race condition between `persistLedgerPath()` and `UpdateConfigLastSync()` in the daemon. They use different config objects:

1. `persistLedgerPath()` loads a **fresh** config from disk via `config.LoadLocalConfig()`, writes `Path = '/correct/path'`, and saves to disk.
2. `UpdateConfigLastSync()` uses the workspace registry's in-memory `localConfigCache`, which still has `Ledger.Path == ''`.
3. When `UpdateConfigLastSync()` saves the stale cache to disk, it **overwrites** the path that `persistLedgerPath()` just wrote.

The sequence:
- Daemon starts, `localConfigCache` loaded with `Ledger == nil`
- `UpdateConfigLastSync('ledger')` creates `LedgerConfig{}` with empty Path in cache, saves to disk → `path = ''` in TOML
- `persistLedgerPath()` loads fresh config from disk, sees `Path == ''`, writes correct path to disk
- Next sync: `UpdateConfigLastSync('ledger')` saves cache (still has `Path == ''`) → overwrites the correct path

## Code Paths

**Daemon (works):** `WorkspaceRegistry.rebuildFromConfigLocked()` skips empty path, falls through to `InitializeLedger()` which computes the default path via `config.DefaultLedgerPath()`. Daemon knows the real path.

**ox status (broken):** `cmd/ox/status.go:1409` checks `localCfg.Ledger == nil` but NOT `localCfg.Ledger.Path == ''`. When the struct exists with empty path, the fallback to `ledger.DefaultPath()` never fires, and the `hasLedger` check at line 535 (`Path \!= ''`) is false → shows 'not cloned'.

## Suggested Fixes

### Fix 1: Root cause — persistLedgerPath should use the registry cache
Add `PersistLedgerPath(path)` method to `WorkspaceRegistry` that updates the `localConfigCache` directly, keeping it in sync with `UpdateConfigLastSync()`. Change `persistLedgerPath()` to call this instead of loading a separate config copy.

### Fix 2: Defensive — ox status should handle empty path
Change `cmd/ox/status.go:1409` from `localCfg.Ledger == nil` to `localCfg.Ledger == nil || localCfg.Ledger.Path == ''` so it falls back to default path discovery.

### Fix 3: Remove unused import
After fix 1, `internal/daemon/sync.go` no longer needs the `config` package import.

## Files Changed

- `internal/daemon/workspace_registry.go` — add `PersistLedgerPath()` method
- `internal/daemon/sync.go` — simplify `persistLedgerPath()`, remove unused config import
- `cmd/ox/status.go` — defensive empty-path fallback

title: PostHog cli.api_call.cli_version is always empty — X-Ox-Version is never sent
description:
apps/api-go/internal/middleware/analytics_middleware.go:33 reads r.Header.Get('X-Ox-Version') and ships it as the cli_version property on every cli.api_call PostHog event.

grep for X-Ox-Version across the entire ox repo returns NOTHING. useragent.SetHeaders sets only User-Agent, X-Orchestrator and traceparent. The header has never been sent.

So cli_version on cli.api_call has been the empty string for every event ever recorded. Any chart or filter built on it reads as 'no data' or silently groups everything into one bucket.

FIX: either have the middleware parse the version out of the User-Agent (cliactivity.ParseOxVersion is already exported for exactly this kind of reuse), or drop the property. Do not leave a field that is structurally always empty.
notes:
ALREADY FIXED server-side on misc-coe branch ajit/misc-coe, commit 8b321224c:
  -"cli_version": r.Header.Get("X-Ox-Version"),
  +"cli_version": cliactivity.ParseOxVersion(r.UserAgent()),
This is the recommended fix — reuse the already-exported UA parser instead of a header ox never sent. ox does NOT need to start sending X-Ox-Version. Not yet merged to main.
close_reason: Fixed server-side on ajit/misc-coe commit 8b321224c; tracking merge separately

title: Daemon polling is recorded as human CLI activity in cli_activity
description:
internal/api/repos.go builds every request with useragent.NewRequest -> useragent.String() = 'ox/<ver> (...)', the CLI User-Agent. The daemon calls GetRepos through that same client (internal/daemon/sync_discovery.go:67,140) for lazy credential refresh, so daemon-originated rows are indistinguishable from a human running ox.

Consequence: an unattended machine with a running daemon can register cli_activity hours with no human present, inflating CLI DAU and cli_hours_active_7d.

Separately, the paths that DO use useragent.DaemonString() ('ox-daemon/<ver> (...)') hit the version regex 'ox/(\\d+...)' in cliactivity.go:34, which does NOT match 'ox-daemon/' -- no literal 'ox/' substring. Those rows get cli_version=''. POST /api/v1/cli/friction from internal/daemon/friction.go:66 is tracked and lands exactly here. GetCLIVersionDistribution filters cli_version != '' so they silently vanish from the version histogram.

DECIDE: should daemon traffic count as CLI activity at all? If no, filter it out explicitly rather than relying on a regex miss. If yes, record a client_class column so daemon and human rows are separable.
notes:
CORRECTION to my earlier note: I assessed the WithDaemonUserAgent doc comment against sageox-monorepo/main and called its premise wrong. It is CORRECT against the branch it ships with. misc-coe (worktree, branch ajit/misc-coe) commit 8b321224c 'fix(analytics): count human CLI activity accurately' adds:

  func IsDaemonUserAgent(ua string) bool {
      return strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(ua), "ox-daemon/")
  }

and short-circuits BOTH middlewares on it — cliactivity.TrackActivity (skips the cli_activity INSERT entirely) and middleware.CLIActivityTracker (skips the cli.api_call PostHog event). Its comment explicitly rejects relying on the ParseOxVersion regex miss: 'the parser's incidental behavior is not an activity policy.' That is the explicit exclusion I said was missing. My criticism applied to main only.

title: ox hook bench: A/B harness for causal measurement of hook impact
description:
The only honest way to claim 'ox hook X saved N tokens' is a counterfactual. This issue ships that counterfactual as a benchmark harness.

Design: user (or CI) provides a fixed task script (e.g., 'add error handling to func F in file G'). Harness runs the same script N times with the target hook enabled, N times disabled. Parses session JSONL for each run. Reports aggregate measured token delta with confidence interval.

Commands:
- ox hook bench run <task.yaml> --hook=pretooluse.read-cache --runs=10
- ox hook bench compare <baseline-run-id> <experiment-run-id>
- ox hook bench list — past benchmark results
- ox hook bench export — JSON for dashboards

Task script format: declarative YAML with task prompt, expected file changes (for correctness gate — runs that fail correctness don't count), success criteria.

Honesty constraints:
- Run count required, default 10, minimum 5 (below that the noise dominates)
- Confidence interval reported alongside mean delta
- Per-run breakdown available so users can audit outlier runs
- Failed runs (didn't produce expected changes) excluded with count surfaced
- RTK-style inverse-effect warning if delta is unfavorable

Reference for why this matters: rtk-ai/rtk issue #582 — PreToolUse hook caused 18% cost INCREASE because Claude generated 50% more output. Only an A/B harness would have caught that pre-ship.

This is slow and expensive to run. Not a per-session command. Designed for: pre-merge gate on hook changes, periodic spot-checks, curious users investigating their own workloads.

Acceptance:
- Task script DSL defined and documented
- Harness orchestrates N runs hook-on, N runs hook-off
- Correctness gate excludes failed runs from token comparison
- Output: mean delta + confidence interval + per-run audit table
- Sample task scripts shipped under examples/
- CI integration story documented
acceptance_criteria: bench harness with task DSL; correctness gate; confidence intervals; sample task scripts; CI integration doc

title: ox cost: parse Claude Code session JSONL for spend visibility
