title: Pre-push gate: unstage-on-fail carve-out for un-redactable session findings
description:
Follow-up to ox-y3ok. When auto-redact-and-retry cannot clear findings (non-JSONL session paths, IO errors, future detector catalog changes), the offending session paths should be carved out of the holding commit so the rest of the push proceeds.

Key design considerations:
- Use 'git reset HEAD~ -- <path>' (or 'git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch -- <path>' when HEAD~ doesn't exist) followed by 'git commit --amend --no-edit --no-verify'.
- Working tree contents preserved (user can manually inspect / redact).
- Daemon anti-entropy interaction: internal/daemon/agentwork/session_finalize.go can re-touch an unstaged session and re-introduce it. Need either (a) a marker the daemon respects to skip re-finalize, or (b) the daemon's session-finalize already skipping non-pointer in-place files (verify behavior).
- Persistent warning surface: ox doctor + ox session stop hook should remind the user.
- Consider whether the unstaged session bytes should also be moved aside (e.g., to .sageox/cache/quarantine/) so the daemon physically can't re-add them.

Acceptance:
- A session with an unfixable finding is carved out of the holding commit; rest of push succeeds; daemon does not re-add it; ox doctor reports the unredacted session under a clear next-step.

title: explore(daemon): replace fsnotify with native FSEvents on macOS to make per-file FD leaks structurally impossible
description: Stronger structural alternative to ox-x60c's userspace-mirror compensation. fsnotify v1.9.0's kqueue backend opens 1+N FDs per watched dir on macOS (1 dir + N per file via watchDirectoryFiles). FSEvents on macOS uses a single FSEventStream per tree — one FD for the whole watch, with kernel-side recursive change notification. Switching macOS to FSEvents directly (or via a thin Go binding) eliminates the per-file FD class entirely: there is nothing to leak because we never opened anything per-file. Linux retains fsnotify/inotify (which is already 1 FD per watch, not per file). Net: better scaling on big monorepos, no kqueue event-buffer pressure, no userspace mirror to maintain. Trade-offs: FSEvents has its own quirks (event coalescing, historical event IDs, slightly different rename semantics), and we'd need a darwin-only build tag plus a Linux/inotify path. Bigger lift than ox-x60c — file as exploration to evaluate whether the structural fix is worth the migration cost. Useful pre-work: prototype with fsnotify/fsevents (https://github.com/fsnotify/fsevents) to measure FD count + latency vs current behavior on a 50k-file repo.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prototype branch with macOS path using FSEvents and Linux path using fsnotify/inotify, behind a build tag. 2) Bench: FD count steady at <50 for an idle daemon on 50k-file repo, vs current >5000+. 3) ox daemon test suite passes on both platforms. 4) Decision doc: ship FSEvents migration vs keep userspace mirror (ox-x60c) — based on measured wins.
notes: Only worth pursuing if ox-x60c's userspace mirror proves insufficient OR if telemetry shows pathological dir counts that make the os.ReadDir cost on startup too high. ox-x60c is correct and version-independent — it's harmless to keep even after this lands. This issue is exploration, not commitment.

title: perf(daemon): bound dirChildren snapshot at maxFilesPerWatchedDir to cap startup memory
description: Open question from the FD-leak fix plan: at startup os.ReadDir runs once per watched dir. For a repo with 10k watched dirs × 50 files avg = 500k stat calls and 500k strings retained in pw.dirChildren. Measurable on cold start. Mitigation: bound dirChildren[path] to maxFilesPerWatchedDir (suggest 10_000). Truncate the slice and log at Warn level when truncated so we can tell from telemetry which dirs are pathological. Truncation is safe-by-degradation: the leak we're fixing is unbounded; bounding the snapshot reintroduces a small bounded leak in exchange for predictable memory. Acceptable tradeoff because (a) any single dir with >10k tracked files is already pathological and likely wants .gitignore tuning, (b) the leak before this whole epic was unbounded. NOT a blocker for shipping ox-x60c — file separately so the core fix can land and we can tune the cap based on real telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: 1) snapshotDirFiles caps the returned slice at maxFilesPerWatchedDir. 2) Truncation logs a single Warn with dir path and total file count. 3) Constant defined as package-level const in project_watcher.go. 4) No regression in ox-lanl regression test.
notes: Decide on the constant value based on observation: instrument first, then tune. Initial guess 10_000 is generous — most engineering repos have <1000 files in any single dir. Consider also a global cap on total tracked children across all dirs as a second-level guard.

title: refactor(daemon): typed watchedDirHandle to centralize Add + child-snapshot + Remove
acceptance_criteria: 1) watchedDirHandle type + acquireDir/Release methods exist in internal/daemon. 2) Start uses defer h.Release() for the root dir. 3) Remove/Rename handler routes through the handle when possible. 4) No behavior change vs ox-x60c — same FD invariants hold. 5) make typecheck && make lint && make test all pass.
notes: Why not RAII: Go's defer is function-scoped and the daemon watcher outlives any single function. runtime.SetFinalizer is GC-timed and unreliable for FDs (the leak this whole epic is fixing is precisely that you cannot bound FD count if cleanup is GC-timed). C++ RAII works because destructors run at scope exit deterministically; Go has no equivalent for resources that must outlive their constructor's scope. The closest reliable Go pattern is context-bound cleanup (defer cancel() / <-ctx.Done()), which is worth adopting if we extend this work.

title: meta.json write race: push-summary vs daemon anti-entropy
description:
WriteSessionMetaOnly performs an atomic file rewrite (tmp + rename), but multiple writers — push-summary, regenerate --redact, doctor repairs, and daemon session-finalize anti-entropy — can race on the same meta.json without coordination. The current code has no file lock or sequence-number guard. A concurrent rewrite can drop a Files entry that another writer just added.

This race exists in the pre-refactor code too (UpdateMetaSummary, redact's WriteSessionMeta) but is more visible now that meta.Files is the single source of truth for which artifacts to stage.

Mitigation options (pick later):
- flock(2) on meta.json during rewrites
- compare-and-swap via stat mtime + retry
- daemon ownership claim before its session-finalize touches the meta

Out of scope for the manifest refactor PR (bd ox-9mrk); filed as follow-up.

title: ox session regenerate --all (default mode) returns 'No sessions found'
description:
## Problem

`ox session regenerate --all --force` (no `--summary`, no `--redact`) returns:

```
No sessions found.
```

…even when the ledger has 80+ sessions whose `summary.md` and `session.md` are stale relative to their `summary.json`. Single-session invocation with the same flags works correctly:

```
$ ox session regenerate <name> --force
✓ Regenerated artifacts for <name>
```

## Repro

`/ox-session-review` on `repo_019c6d2e-27b0-798d-aaed-b036114dc63a` (sageox-mono ledger), 2026-04-25:
- 80+ sessions known to need .md backfill from existing summary.json
- `ox session regenerate --all --force` → "No sessions found"
- Per-name invocation succeeded for 10/12 sessions tested.

## Root cause hypothesis

The `--all` filter in default mode is probably scoped to "sessions that need redaction" or "sessions modified by `ox session push` since last regen", missing the much larger set of sessions whose .md artifacts are stale relative to their summary.json.

## Fix direction

Either:
- Tighten the help text to document what `--all` actually selects in default mode (current help: `--all  regenerate all sessions` overstates).
- Broaden the default-mode `--all` filter to include all sessions where `mtime(summary.md) < mtime(summary.json)` OR `summary.md` is missing.

Option 2 is preferable — it makes `--all` actually match a user's mental model and unblocks the night-watchman backfill path (sageox/sageox-monorepo#1008).

title: Legacy inline-stored sessions — raw.jsonl committed inline, never LFS-uploaded
description:
## Problem

Pre-LFS sessions (or sessions that finalized with an empty `files: {}` manifest) have their `raw.jsonl` committed inline as a regular blob (49–64 KB observed) instead of as an LFS pointer. They have no LFS OID, no `files` manifest entry, and currently land in the `meta_repair` bucket on audit.

## Repro

`/ox-session-review` on `repo_019c6d2e-27b0-798d-aaed-b036114dc63a` (sageox-mono ledger), 2026-04-25:
- `2026-04-24T19-24-ajit-Oxj32z` (43 entries, 49605-byte inline blob, `files: {}`)
- `2026-04-24T21-10-ryan-Ox5SS5` (84 entries, 64838-byte inline blob, `files: {}`)

## Why it matters

- Bloats ledger git history with binary content that should be in LFS.
- Confuses anti-entropy passes (looks like a missing-manifest error when actually the data is right there inline).
- Future LFS-only readers will fail on these sessions.

## Fix direction

One-shot migration tool, e.g. `ox session migrate-to-lfs <name>`:
1. Detect inline `raw.jsonl` (blob > N bytes AND no `files` manifest entry).
2. Compute SHA256 of inline content.
3. Upload to LFS via Batch API in `internal/lfs/client.go`.
4. Replace inline blob with LFS pointer file.
5. Update `meta.json.files` with the new manifest entry.
6. Commit as `migrate: <name> raw.jsonl → LFS`.

Should be runnable as part of the night-watchman session-ledger audit (sageox/sageox-monorepo#1008) under the `meta_repair` bucket once the inline-detection signal is added.

title: Ghost session in CLI listing — listed by ox session list but no on-disk dir
description:
## Problem

`ox session list --all` returns session names that have no corresponding directory under the ledger's `sessions/` path. `ox session remove <name> --force` then errors with `no sessions found matching "<name>"`, leaving the entry permanently undeleteable from the CLI.

## Repro

Found during `/ox-session-review` on `repo_019c6d2e-27b0-798d-aaed-b036114dc63a` (sageox-mono ledger), 2026-04-25:
- Session `2026-03-22T21-47-ryan-Oxwqyu` listed by `ox session list --all`
- No dir at `~/.local/share/sageox/sageox.ai/ledgers/repo_019c6d2e.../sessions/2026-03-22T21-47-ryan-Oxwqyu/`
- `ox session remove 2026-03-22T21-47-ryan-Oxwqyu --force` → `Error: no sessions found matching ...`

## Root cause hypothesis

CLI listing source (likely a server/index query or a stale local cache) is not reconciled against on-disk state.

## Fix direction

- `ox session list` should self-heal: filter out names where the on-disk session dir is missing, OR surface them with a `status: ghost` flag and a `--prune-ghosts` action.
- `ox session remove` should accept ghost names and clean the index entry without requiring an on-disk dir.

title: feat(tokenstrip): opt-in token-aware compaction stage for sessionpipeline
description:
New pkg/tokenstrip package implementing sessionpipeline.Stage. Reduces TOKEN count (not bytes) via tokenizer-aware transforms. Explicitly lossy; off by default; toggled via OX_SUMMARY_INPUT_TOKEN_STRIP=on or --token-strip flag.

Stage ordering when enabled:
  raw → tokenopt (drop system, compact tools) → tokenstrip (opt-in) → summarizer

Scope — safe transforms first (v1):
  - Unicode NFC normalization (golang.org/x/text/unicode/norm) — lossless, tiny win
  - Zero-width / unusual whitespace strip — lossless
  - Whitespace canonicalization in assistant prose — near-lossless
  - Stop-word removal STRICTLY inside assistant <thinking> blocks only — lossy but safe scope
  - Synonym substitution for high-token phrases ('configuration' → 'config') in assistant reasoning only — configurable table

Must never touch:
  - User turns (intent signal is sacred)
  - Assistant final prose (the answer to the user)
  - Tool names or tool inputs (summarizer scaffolding)

Dependencies:
  - tiktoken-go (approximate Claude tokenization for sizing)
  - bbalet/stopwords (ISO-639 aware stop word lists)
  - golang.org/x/text/unicode/norm
  No Go port of LLMLingua/LongLLMLingua exists today; intentional non-goal.

Blocked by: ox-ugvy (summary-quality eval harness). No measurable way to verify this doesn't degrade summaries until eval exists. Do not ship before that.
close_reason: Shipped as pkg/tokenstrip on PR #553 branch. 5 transforms: NFC normalization, zero-width strip, whitespace canon, stop-words in thinking blocks, opt-in synonyms. 18 tests, all sacred rules test-enforced (never touches user/non-thinking/tool fields). Off by default. Conforms to tokenopt's shape for one-line sessionpipeline.Stage adoption when that package merges.

title: refactor: split processAgentSession into named phase functions
description:
cmd/ox/agent_session.go processAgentSession is ~500 lines of linear orchestration covering: read cache entries, redact, validate, write raw.jsonl, write meta.json, write artifacts, upload pipeline, summary prompt build, telemetry emission. Pass-by-side-effect via *agentSessionResult.

Proposed split (no new types, no interfaces — just named functions in the same file):
  - finalizePhase: read cache → redact → validate → write raw.jsonl + meta.json
  - compressPhase: existing writeOptimizedJSONLForSummary + stats plumbing
  - summarizePhase: BuildSummaryPrompt + SummaryPrompt return path
  - artifactsPhase: WriteSessionArtifacts + ledger copy
  - telemetryPhase: emit session-end event

processAgentSession becomes a ~50-line orchestrator calling them in order.

REVIEWER DISAGREEMENT noted: refactoring-specialist said do it (independent testability + readability); backend-architect said defer (linear is readable, break when a second caller exists). Taste call. If no second caller emerges, this is optional. File to track the question, not committing to do it.

title: cleanup: delete dead pkg/sessionsummary.FilterForSummarization

Delete, don't deprecate. No external consumers. If a future transform wants similar filtering, it'll be a fresh implementation at a call site with current knowledge — the existing one reflects assumptions that no longer hold (e.g., it decided to filter Read/Glob/Grep as 'exploratory noise', a decision superseded by tokenopt's ConversationOnly mode keeping every tool as a tool_mark).

~50 lines deleted from pkg/sessionsummary. Update imports and tests.

description:

Convert to streaming and implement pkg/sessionpipeline.Stage once the LLM redactor ships as the SECOND streaming transform. Rewriting before that point has no ROI — the existing slice API works fine for a single-caller in-memory scenario. The rewrite becomes worthwhile when (a) pipeline reordering is desired (e.g., pattern-redact AFTER compress for token savings), or (b) fast-and-llm redactors want to compose cleanly.

Depends on: LLM redactor bead landing first. Do not do this before.

title: Runtime guard in ConfigureSparseCheckout against missing .sageox
description:
ConfigureSparseCheckout constructs a dirs slice and passes it to git sparse-checkout set. If .sageox is ever missing from that slice (due to a future refactor or dynamic construction bug), the entire .sageox/cache/ tree is silently deleted.

What needs to change:
- Add a runtime assertion at the top of ConfigureSparseCheckout: if .sageox is not in dirs, return a hard error instead of proceeding
- This turns a silent data-destroying git call into a loud programming error
- The existing regression tests (TestConfigureSparseCheckout_PreservesBleveCacheWhenSageoxNotPreviouslyInCone etc.) already catch this statically; the runtime guard catches dynamic construction paths the tests don't cover

Why: Defense in depth. The tests from PR #364 cover the current static dirs slice. A runtime guard covers future code paths where dirs might be constructed dynamically (e.g. from config, flags, or merged with external cone state).

Acceptance: Calling ConfigureSparseCheckout with a dirs slice missing .sageox returns an error without running git. Test added.

title: Research: Bleve-SQLite virtual table bridge (Tantivy-SQLite parity)
description:
Deep dive research into whether ox should implement a Bleve-SQLite virtual table bridge, mirroring CodeDB's Tantivy-SQLite architecture.

Current state: CodeDB exposes Tantivy as SQLite virtual tables (code_search(), diff_search()) so SQLite's optimizer builds unified execution plans across both engines in a single query. ox uses Bleve as a separate engine queried independently, then intersects results in Go code (search/planner.go JoinIntersect strategy).

Questions to answer:
1. What predicate pushdown opportunities are we losing? (e.g., can SQLite push file/lang filters into the FTS query?)
2. How much does the Go-side intersection cost in practice? Profile with large result sets.
3. Does modernc.org/sqlite support custom virtual tables in pure Go? What's the API surface?
4. What would the implementation look like? (Bleve adapter implementing sqlite vtab interface)
5. Is the engineering cost justified given current search latency (~68ms)?
6. Are there simpler wins (e.g., pushing more filters into Bleve queries before intersection)?

This is research only — no implementation. Produce a written recommendation with benchmarks.

Acceptance: Written analysis with profiling data, architectural tradeoffs, and go/no-go recommendation.

Decision needed: is Pi (shittycodingagent.ai) worth supporting as an adapter, or should we drop the stub?

title: Add 5th prompt variant to attribution-guidance and subagent-discovery
description: CodeRabbit review on PR #41 noted that attribution-guidance and subagent-discovery each have 4 Texts entries while iterationsPerQuery=5. This means variant 0 runs twice (4%4==0), giving it double weight. Add a 5th phrasing to each for uniform coverage.

title: Update Makefile benchmark cost/time comment
description: The Makefile test-benchmark target comment says '~36 min, ~18 API calls' but with the new 8 queries x 5 iterations it's now ~40 API calls, ~80 min. Update the comment to reflect accurate numbers.
close_reason: Updated Makefile comment and timeout

title: Config setting for session publish mode (auto/manual)
description: Add a config setting 'session.publishing' with values 'auto' (default, current behavior) and 'manual'. In manual mode, session stop saves locally but does not push to ledger. User explicitly pushes with 'ox session upload' or similar. This gives full control over what gets shared. Config location: .sageox/config.json or user config. Future work - keep it simple for now.
